css.at-rules.charset.note: Style sheets are read as UTF-8.

css.at-rules.container.note: Size queries (width, height, inline-size, block-size, aspect-ratio, orientation, with the range syntax) on the nearest container that can answer them, by name or not, measured on the last frame; style() queries test the computed values of the nearest ancestor, or of the nearest one with the name: style(--x: value), style(--x), with not, and or or; size and style conditions joined by and both pass, each on the nearest container it applies to, or on the one of the name.

css.at-rules.container.scroll-state.note: scroll-state() queries on the nearest scroll-state container (container-type: scroll-state), by name or not, as it was drawn in the last frame: stuck (a sticky element stuck to the top or the bottom), snapped (a snap target its scroll container rests on, x or y), scrollable (the sides a scroll container can be scrolled to) and scrolled (the side it was last scrolled to), with not, and or or.

css.at-rules.counter-style.note: Every system (cyclic, numeric, alphabetic, symbolic, additive, fixed, extends) with symbols, additive-symbols, negative, prefix, suffix, range, pad and fallback, for list-style-type, ::marker and counter(); symbols are text, not images; a later rule of a name replaces an earlier one.

css.at-rules.custom-media.note: A name for a media query list, tested by (--name) in @media and @import, defined before or after its use; true and false are queries that always and never match; an undefined name never matches.

css.at-rules.font-face.note: The terminal draws text with its own font: fonts cannot be loaded.

css.at-rules.font-feature-values.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.at-rules.font-palette-values.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.at-rules.function.note: Custom functions, like --double(2ch): typed parameters with defaults, local custom properties, the last result, in @media and @supports rules too, a return type; called in any property and in custom properties, the custom properties of the element seen; a call that fails, a cycle or a value not of its type make the declaration invalid at computed-value time.

css.at-rules.import.note: Resolved with the stylesheet loader; a media list is honored.

css.at-rules.keyframes.note: from, to and percentages; colors and numbers are interpolated, also in lists and functions of the same shape (1ch 2ch, translate(), a shadow and its color, a gradient), lengths of different units through calc(); other values change halfway, like CSS discrete animation.

css.at-rules.layer.note: Named, nested and anonymous layers, statements and @import layer(); unlayered rules win over layered ones, and !important reverses the order, like CSS.

css.at-rules.media.note: Media types all, screen and tty match; others never do.

css.at-rules.media.aspect-ratio.note: Uses the pixel size of the terminal.

css.at-rules.media.color.note: Bits per component: 8 with true colors, 2 with 256 colors, 1 with 16, 0 when forced off; from MediaContext, COLORTERM and TERM by default.

css.at-rules.media.color-gamut.note: srgb, unless colors are forced off.

css.at-rules.media.color-index.note: 256 or 16 with a palette, 0 with true colors.

css.at-rules.media.device-aspect-ratio.note: The terminal is the device: like aspect-ratio.

css.at-rules.media.device-height.note: The terminal is the device: like height.

css.at-rules.media.device-width.note: The terminal is the device: like width.

css.at-rules.media.forced-colors.note: Active when NO_COLOR is set or colors are disabled.

css.at-rules.media.grid.note: Always 1: a terminal is a grid device.

css.at-rules.media.height.note: In rows; px are converted with the cell pixel size.

css.at-rules.media.hover.note: "hover" when the application tracks the mouse (MediaContext::withPointer()), "none" otherwise.

css.at-rules.media.monochrome.note: Matches when colors are forced off.

css.at-rules.media.orientation.note: Uses the pixel size of the terminal.

css.at-rules.media.pointer.note: "fine" when the application tracks the mouse, "none" otherwise; never "coarse".

css.at-rules.media.prefers-color-scheme.note: From MediaContext: set by the application, COLORFGBG by default.

css.at-rules.media.prefers-reduced-trans.note: Always no-preference: translucent colors are blended, none made opaque.

css.at-rules.media.resolution.note: dppx, x, dpi and dpcm, from the cell pixel size.

css.at-rules.media.width.note: In columns; px are converted with the cell pixel size.

css.at-rules.namespace.note: Elements are in the HTML namespace: a prefix declared or not matches none of them in selectors, *| matches them all.

css.at-rules.position-try.note: Named fallbacks for position-try-fallbacks: their insets (with anchor()), position-area and position-anchor place the element when its own place would leave the screen, at the width and height they set (lengths or anchor-size()), with which it must fit; their other sizes and margins are ignored; a later rule of a name replaces an earlier one.

css.at-rules.property.note: Registers a custom property: inherits: false keeps it on the element that sets it, initial-value is its value where nothing sets it, and a typed syntax (<color>, <length>, <number>, <percentage>...) lets it be transitioned and animated; a value not of the syntax is invalid at computed-value time, inherited or initial, and an initial value not of it invalidates the registration.

css.at-rules.scope.note: A root and a limit, or the element of the <style> without a root: the rules match in its subtree, not in or below the limit, with no specificity added, :scope being the root; the root itself matches through :scope only.

css.at-rules.starting-style.note: The values the transitions of an element start from when it is first shown, or shown again after display: none; nested in rules too.

css.at-rules.supports.note: A declaration is supported when it has an effect; selector() is supported.

css.at-rules.view-transition.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.properties.-moz-osx-font-smoothing.note: The terminal draws the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.-ms-overflow-style.note: Scrollbars are drawn by the scroll containers, see scrollbar-width.

css.properties.-webkit-backdrop-filter.note: What is behind an element is not filtered; see filter.

css.properties.-webkit-box-align.note: A -webkit-box is a block: see display: flex.

css.properties.-webkit-box-direction.note: A -webkit-box is a block: see display: flex.

css.properties.-webkit-box-flex.note: A -webkit-box is a block: see display: flex.

css.properties.-webkit-box-orient.note: A -webkit-box is a block, its children one under the other: see -webkit-line-clamp.

css.properties.-webkit-box-pack.note: A -webkit-box is a block: see display: flex.

css.properties.-webkit-font-smoothing.note: The terminal draws the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.-webkit-line-clamp.note: Like line-clamp; display: -webkit-box and -webkit-box-orient are not needed.

css.properties.-webkit-overflow-scrollin.note: Scrolling follows the keys and the wheel: there is no momentum.

css.properties.-webkit-text-fill-color.note: The color of the glyphs, over color: currentcolor, borders and outlines keep color; inherited; transparent text takes the color behind it.

css.properties.-webkit-text-stroke.note: A cell has one foreground color: the outline of a glyph cannot be drawn.

css.properties.-webkit-text-stroke-color.note: A cell has one foreground color: the outline of a glyph cannot be drawn.

css.properties.-webkit-text-stroke-width.note: A cell has one foreground color: the outline of a glyph cannot be drawn.

css.properties.-webkit-user-drag.note: Elements are not dragged and dropped.

css.properties.accent-color.note: Colors the box of checkboxes and radios and the filled part of progress bars.

css.properties.align-content.note: The lines of a wrapped row and the rows of a grid of a set height share its free rows: start, center, end, space-between, space-around, space-evenly and stretch (normal: stretch for lines, start for grid rows, whose auto rows stretch takes as even shares).

css.properties.align-items.note: start, center and end; in rows, stretch (the default) pads the shorter items to the height of the row, that of the container when it has a set height, like a single-line flex container; in flex columns, the items not stretched are as wide as their content, placed across; baseline is like start (rows have one height), last baseline like end.

css.properties.align-self.note: start, center, end and stretch: in rows, the item within the height of the row; in flex columns, across: an item not stretched is as wide as its content; baseline is like start. anchor-center centers an element placed next to its anchor down it, see justify-self.

css.properties.alignment-baseline.note: The shapes of an <svg> are not drawn with it, from a style sheet or an attribute: see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.all.note: initial, inherit, unset, revert (to the user agent value) and revert-layer (like revert) for every property but the custom ones, direction and unicode-bidi.

css.properties.anchor-name.note: A dashed name absolute and fixed elements are placed next to, see position-anchor; the first name of a list.

css.properties.anchor-scope.note: all or a list of dashed names: an absolute or fixed element outside the element does not see those names on it nor inside it, like the repeated cards of a list each anchoring their own tooltip.

css.properties.animation.note: Every animation of the list, up to 16, a later one winning on the properties both animate: name, duration, timing (see the easing functions), delay, iteration count, direction, fill mode and play state; drawn at about 30 frames a second, smooth ones in 32 steps.

css.properties.animation-composition.note: A list, one value per animation-name: add and accumulate add the keyframes set to the element's value, numbers of the same unit and colors channel by channel, the keyframes missing being its value; other values are replaced.

css.properties.animation-delay.note: A list, one value per animation-name, repeated when shorter; see animation.

css.properties.animation-direction.note: A list, one value per animation-name, repeated when shorter; see animation.

css.properties.animation-duration.note: A list, one value per animation-name, repeated when shorter; see animation.

css.properties.animation-fill-mode.note: A list, one value per animation-name, repeated when shorter; see animation.

css.properties.animation-iteration-count.note: A list, one value per animation-name, repeated when shorter; see animation.

css.properties.animation-name.note: A list, one value per animation-name, repeated when shorter; see animation.

css.properties.animation-play-state.note: A list, one value per animation-name, repeated when shorter; see animation.

css.properties.animation-range.note: normal, cover, contain, entry and exit, with percentages, on view timelines; on scroll timelines normal and percentages.

css.properties.animation-range-end.note: normal, cover, contain, entry and exit, with percentages, on view timelines; on scroll timelines normal and percentages.

css.properties.animation-range-start.note: normal, cover, contain, entry and exit, with percentages, on view timelines; on scroll timelines normal and percentages.

css.properties.animation-timeline.note: auto, none, scroll() (nearest, root or self; block, inline, y or x), view() (block, inline, y or x) or the name of a scroll-timeline or view-timeline: the animation goes with where its scroll container is scrolled, as it was laid out in the last frame, its duration and delay not used; view() and view timelines from where the element enters the scroll container to where it leaves it.

css.properties.animation-timing-function.note: A list, one value per animation-name, repeated when shorter; see animation.

css.properties.appearance.note: none draws a button without its brackets, a checkbox or radio without its box (only its ::before and ::after content, like a ✓ from input:checked::before; without content, a box of CSS too short for its border, like the 1em one of Bootstrap, is a mark, ☐ ☑ or ○ ◉, in the color of its border, or of its background once checked) a select without its ▾ marker and a textarea without the rules above and below its text, which a border the page gives it replaces too, like the textareas of Bootstrap; base-select draws a select as a dropdown without the brackets of its field, its ::picker-icon kept and its ::picker(select) styled; the other values draw their own look.

css.properties.aspect-ratio.note: A ratio (16 / 9) or a number: a box without a height is as tall as its width says, cells being twice as tall as wide, the percentage heights of its children of that height; an image keeps it too; auto is its content.

css.properties.backdrop-filter.note: What is behind an element is not filtered; see filter.

css.properties.backface-visibility.note: Cells cannot be rotated nor scaled: there is no 3D space; see translate.

css.properties.background.note: The color and an image, a url() or a gradient, with its position / size, repeat and boxes (the origin and the clip, or the origin then the clip), of each layer, the first one over the others, see background-image; not the attachment.

css.properties.background-blend-mode.note: The background image or gradient blended with the background color, cell by cell, see the blend modes; a mode per layer, the list repeated past its end: each layer blended with the layers under it and the background color.

css.properties.background-clip.note: border-box, padding-box and content-box: the cells the background color, image and gradient are painted in; text paints them as the color of the glyphs, as with a transparent text color, the cells keeping what is behind them.

css.properties.background-image.note: url() images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP... with the GD extension, and SVG, its currentColor black, strokes thinner than half a cell fading out, like the close button of Bootstrap), from a data: URL or the stylesheet loader, two pixels per cell: half blocks in the spaces, the average of the two under the characters; linear-gradient() (an angle or to a side or corner), radial-gradient() (a circle or an ellipse, of a size, at a position), conic-gradient() (from an angle, around a position) and their repeating forms, color stops with percentages, lengths, or angles around a conic one. Every image of a list, up to 8, the first one over the others, each with its own position, size, repeat and boxes (a list shorter than them repeating), their translucent colors blended over the layers under them, over the background color (with background-clip: text, the first one alone); forced colors draw no image, and the first color of a gradient.

css.properties.background-origin.note: border-box, padding-box (the initial value) and content-box: the area the image or gradient is sized and placed in.

css.properties.background-position.note: Keywords, lengths and percentages, one to four values with offsets from an edge, like right 2ch bottom 1; one per layer, see background-image.

css.properties.background-repeat.note: repeat, no-repeat, space and round, by axis, repeat-x and repeat-y: the image or gradient tiles its painting area from its position; space spreads whole tiles across the positioning area.

css.properties.background-size.note: Lengths and percentages of the positioning area, one or two; auto is the size of an image (8 pixels per column, two per row), keeping its proportions when the other one is set, or the area for a gradient, which has none of its own; cover and contain scale an image to the area, keeping its proportions, and make a gradient the size of the area.

css.properties.baseline-shift.note: The shapes of an <svg> are not drawn with it, from a style sheet or an attribute: see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.baseline-source.note: The characters of a row share one baseline.

css.properties.block-size.note: Like height in a horizontal writing mode, like width in a vertical one.

css.properties.border.note: Any width above 0 draws a one-cell border, thick ones with heavy lines; dashed and dotted have their own lines, groove, ridge, inset and outset are solid. The lines of a box right under another join those of the other where they go on from them, like the items of a list group, └ over │ making ├. An empty ::before, ::after or element drawn by its borders, one side of a color and one beside it transparent, like the caret of a dropdown of Bootstrap, is a triangle pointing away from that side, ▾ ▴ ▸ ◂, in its color.

css.properties.border-block.note: The width, style and color of the sides; any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-color.note: Logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-end.note: The width, style and color of the sides; any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-end-color.note: Logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-end-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-end-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-start.note: The width, style and color of the sides; any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-start-color.note: Logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-start-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-start-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-block-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-bottom.note: The width, style and color of the side; any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.border-bottom-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side.

css.properties.border-bottom-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.border-collapse.note: collapse draws a table and its cells as one grid of lines, with junctions, the table as wide as its columns, or as its width, the columns sharing the room left as they are wide; a line is drawn where the table, a row group, a row or a cell beside it has a border on that side, like the border-bottom of cells drawing the lines under rows only, in the style and color of the table, or of the first border; a table whose rows are displayed as blocks, like those of EasyAdmin on a narrow screen, lays them out like blocks.

css.properties.border-color.note: One to four colors, by side; the corners take the color of the top or bottom side.

css.properties.border-image.note: Its source, see border-image-source; the slice, width, outset and repeat are accepted: a border is a line of cells.

css.properties.border-image-outset.note: Accepted: the border keeps its width, a line of cells, see border-width.

css.properties.border-image-repeat.note: Accepted: the source stretches over the border.

css.properties.border-image-slice.note: Accepted: the whole source colors the border, a line of cells.

css.properties.border-image-source.note: A gradient or a url() image, see background-image: the lines of the border take its colors, cell by cell, the average of the two pixels of a cell of an image; none removes it; forced colors keep the border color.

css.properties.border-image-width.note: Accepted: the border keeps its width, a line of cells, see border-width.

css.properties.border-inline.note: The width, style and color of the sides; any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-color.note: Logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-end.note: The width, style and color of the sides; any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-end-color.note: Logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-end-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-end-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-start.note: The width, style and color of the sides; any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-start-color.note: Logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-start-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-start-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-inline-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell; logical sides follow direction, in a top-to-bottom writing mode.

css.properties.border-left.note: The width, style and color of the side; any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.border-left-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side.

css.properties.border-left-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.border-radius.note: One to four radii, by corner; any radius above 0 rounds that corner of a solid border (╭), the elliptic radii after a slash are not needed; see corner-shape.

css.properties.border-right.note: The width, style and color of the side; any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.border-right-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side.

css.properties.border-right-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.border-spacing.note: The first length sets how far apart the cells of a separate table are across, 0 making their borders touch, like the files of GitHub; without it they are a column apart, see the gap of tr in the user agent stylesheet. The second is accepted, the rows touching.

css.properties.border-style.note: One to four styles, by side, like the other box sides; Tui patterns (rounded, tall, wide...) are accepted too.

css.properties.border-top.note: The width, style and color of the side; any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.border-top-style.note: none removes the side; the corners join the styles of their sides when box drawing has a glyph for them (light and heavy, single and double), else take the style of the top or bottom side.

css.properties.border-top-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.border-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell; thick draws heavy lines.

css.properties.bottom.note: In cells or percents of the containing block of an absolute or fixed element (top: 100% puts it below), also in calc(), min(), max() and clamp(), like left: calc(50% - 10ch); top and bottom also place a sticky one.

css.properties.box-decoration-break.note: On inline elements: slice, the default, draws the left padding and border on the first line of an element that wraps and the right ones on its last line; clone draws them on each of its lines. On blocks cut across the columns of a multi-column container: slice draws the top edge in the first piece and the bottom one in the last, clone draws both edges around each piece.

css.properties.box-orient.note: A -webkit-box is a block, its children one under the other: see -webkit-line-clamp.

css.properties.box-shadow.note: A shadow spread around the box, not moved nor blurred, like a focus ring, is a line hugging the box from outside, over the blank cells around it (not the text nor the lines), thin up to 2px, else thick, the widest of them, unless an outline is drawn; an inset one of a few pixels is the same line along the edge cells of the box, inside it, over the blank ones, like the frame of the notes of PHP.net, or around a box of less than three rows, like a field with the ring-inset of Tailwind; the first other shadow that is not inset: its offsets, blur and spread rounded to whole cells, from three quarters of one, so that a shadow of a pixel or two, a hairline in browsers, is none (its offsets 0 to 4, to the right and below), take room between the border and the margin, in its color blended over what is behind; the first inset one shades the edges inside the border it is offset from (top and left, or bottom and right when negative), the text staying; one not moved nor blurred with a spread of a hundred cells or more, like the inset 0 0 0 9999px of the stripes of a table of Bootstrap, is a background over the background color, blended with it, under the border too. Outside, the spread grows the shadow on the right and below (not past the top and left of the box, where it has no room), and a blur adds a softer cell around it, drawn with half blocks in its color; inside, blur and spread are ignored.

css.properties.box-sizing.note: border-box, the widths and heights set including the padding and the border, is the initial value, like the common reset; content-box adds them to the widths and heights set.

css.properties.break-after.note: column (and page, always, left, right) starts a column before or after the element in a multi-column container, within its column count; avoid keeps it in the column of its neighbour.

css.properties.break-before.note: column (and page, always, left, right) starts a column before or after the element in a multi-column container, within its column count; avoid keeps it in the column of its neighbour.

css.properties.break-inside.note: avoid and avoid-column keep the element in one column of a multi-column ancestor, unless it is taller than a column; avoid-page is like avoid.

css.properties.caption-side.note: The caption above or below its table, collapsed or separate.

css.properties.caret.note: Its color, shape and animation, see caret-color, caret-shape and caret-animation.

css.properties.caret-animation.note: manual: the caret of the terminal does not blink; auto, the default, lets it blink.

css.properties.caret-color.note: The terminal cursor takes the color while a field has the focus (OSC 12), given back to the terminal (OSC 112) otherwise and on exit; auto, the default, and transparent keep the color of the terminal cursor; the 16 ANSI colors are sent in their xterm shades.

css.properties.clear.note: The element goes below the floats before it on that side.

css.properties.clip.note: A rect() without width or height leaves nothing to see, like the visually hidden pattern (.sr-only): the element is not drawn, its text staying in the names of what holds it; other rects are ignored, a box being a rectangle of cells.

css.properties.clip-path.note: inset() of half the box or more, or a rect() without width or height, like the rect(0 0 0 0) of the .sr-only of GitHub, leaves nothing to see, like the visually hidden pattern: the element is not drawn; other shapes are ignored, a box being a rectangle of cells. On the shapes and groups of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them and their style attribute, url() of a <clipPath>: what they draw is clipped to the union of its shapes (rect, circle, ellipse, polygon, path... and the copies of <use>, not text), in their user space or, with clipPathUnits="objectBoundingBox", the box of a shape; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.clip-rule.note: nonzero or evenodd: the inside of the shapes of a <clipPath>. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.color-adjust.note: The old name of print-color-adjust: nothing is printed.

css.properties.color-interpolation.note: The shapes of an <svg> are not drawn with it, from a style sheet or an attribute: see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.color-interpolation-filte.note: The shapes of an <svg> are not drawn with it, from a style sheet or an attribute: see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.color-scheme.note: light or dark alone forces that scheme on the element and its descendants for light-dark(); light dark, both, and normal follow prefers-color-scheme.

css.properties.column-count.note: The content of a container flows into that many balanced columns, filled one after the other, the last one shorter: blocks are cut between columns between their lines, as orphans and widows allow, and between the blocks they hold; images, form controls, flex rows and grids are not cut, and neither are the edges of a box from its first and last lines.

css.properties.column-fill.note: balance (and balance-all) shares the content evenly between the columns; auto fills them one after the other up to the height of the container, taller when the content does not fit, balanced without a height or max-height, like browsers.

css.properties.column-gap.note: Used when it matches the layout direction; grid-row-gap and grid-column-gap, their old names, too.

css.properties.column-rule.note: A line between the columns, in the middle of the gap, in the style (solid, dashed, dotted, double) and color; the width is one cell.

css.properties.column-rule-width.note: Any width above 0 is one cell.

css.properties.column-span.note: all: a child of the multi-column container spans its columns, the content before and after it in columns of their own.

css.properties.column-width.note: As many columns as fit at that least width, at most column-count.

css.properties.columns.note: A count and a least width, see column-count and column-width.

css.properties.contain.note: size and strict size the element by contain-intrinsic-size, its content drawn in that size, cut at it; inline-size its width alone; without a size there, nothing changes, as the content would go over what follows; layout, style, paint and content are hints for browsers.

css.properties.contain-intrinsic-size.note: The width and the height of the content of an element with content-visibility: hidden or contain: size (its content drawn in that size), and no width or height; auto is the size given, nothing being remembered.

css.properties.container-type.note: size and inline-size make the element a container for @container size queries; a query on the block axis (height, block-size, aspect-ratio, orientation) skips the inline-size containers for a size one further up; scroll-state, alone or with one of them, for scroll-state() queries.

css.properties.content.note: On ::before and ::after of text blocks and inline elements, and on li::marker: strings, attr(), counters, quotes and url() images, drawn in the line a row tall and as wide as their proportions say (nothing for one that cannot be read); ::before and ::after of a block holding blocks are lines of their own, before and after them, in the style of the pseudo-element (inline in its text when it starts or ends with text); in a flex row or a grid, items of their own, placed like the others.

css.properties.content-visibility.note: hidden draws the box without its children or its text, which take neither the focus nor the pointer, sized by contain-intrinsic-size; auto is like visible: what is not on the screen costs nothing already.

css.properties.corner-block-end-shape.note: The two corners of a side, see corner-shape.

css.properties.corner-block-start-shape.note: The two corners of a side, see corner-shape.

css.properties.corner-bottom-shape.note: The two corners of a side, see corner-shape.

css.properties.corner-inline-end-shape.note: The two corners of a side, see corner-shape.

css.properties.corner-inline-start-shape.note: The two corners of a side, see corner-shape.

css.properties.corner-left-shape.note: The two corners of a side, see corner-shape.

css.properties.corner-right-shape.note: The two corners of a side, see corner-shape.

css.properties.corner-shape.note: One to four shapes, by corner, of the corners with a radius above 0: round, squircle and superellipse() above 0 draw ╭, square and superellipse(infinity) the corner of the border, bevel, notch, scoop and superellipse() of 0 or below draw a diagonal (╱), the cells being too coarse for the others.

css.properties.corner-top-shape.note: The two corners of a side, see corner-shape.

css.properties.counter-reset.note: With the CSS scoping: a counter is seen by the element, its descendants and its following siblings.

css.properties.cursor.note: The keyword, for HtmlView::cursorAt(): the application sets the pointer shape (OSC 22); url() images are skipped for the fallback keyword.

css.properties.custom-property.note: Cascades and inherits; read with var(); initial is the guaranteed-invalid value, var() taking its fallback, and unset inherits, like CSS.

css.properties.cx.note: The center of a <circle> or an <ellipse>, in user units, a unit or a percentage of the viewBox. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.cy.note: The center of a <circle> or an <ellipse>, in user units, a unit or a percentage of the viewBox. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.d.note: The outline of a <path>: none or path() of its commands. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.direction.note: rtl: logical sides (inline start and end) are the right and left ones, rows and grids run from the right, text and blocks start on the right; the lines of text are drawn in visual order by the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9), with ext-intl or symfony/polyfill-intl-char, otherwise as stored, the terminal reordering them or not, and as stored in the terminals that reorder them themselves (Terminal.app, Konsole, mlterm); the text of inputs and textareas, each of its lines in the direction of its first strong character, the cursor with the character it is on.

css.properties.display.note:
none hides; contents has no box, its children laid out in its parent; flex lays children out in a row unless flex-direction says otherwise, its items sized by their content unless they grow. Inline children of a block that some rule makes a flex container, in any media, become flex items, those of a text block like

or

  • too, its text runs items of their own. inline-block, inline-flex and inline-grid with a border are boxed in the line of the text around them, like a button, as wide as their content, and with a width, at that width, like the bars of the placeholders of Bootstrap; a block element displayed inline-block, inline-flex or inline-grid by the rules of every media and state, like
    , is in the line too, as wide as its content, and stays a block when some media or state makes it one; one displayed inline by the rules of every media and state, like the
  • of a breadcrumb, is text of the line, unless it holds a block or a form control. table, table-row-group (and the header and footer groups), table-row and table-cell size the columns across the rows, table-column and table-column-group give them a least width; a caption, or display: table-caption, is drawn above its table, or below it by caption-side, the table at least as wide as its longest word. A block of rows, like table { display: block; overflow-x: auto } to scroll a wide table, is drawn as their table, like the anonymous table of CSS.

css.properties.dominant-baseline.note: The shapes of an <svg> are not drawn with it, from a style sheet or an attribute: see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.dynamic-range-limit.note: Colors are sent to the terminal as they are.

css.properties.empty-cells.note: hide: in a separate table, a cell without content draws no border nor background, keeping its room; inherited, so set on the table; collapsed tables draw every cell, like CSS.

css.properties.field-sizing.note: content lets a textarea grow with its content past its rows, and makes a text input as wide as its value (or its placeholder) and the cursor, within its width; fixed, the default, keeps a textarea at its rows, scrolling, and an input at its width.

css.properties.fill.note: A color, currentColor, none, or a gradient or a pattern by url(). On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.fill-opacity.note: A number or a percentage. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.fill-rule.note: nonzero or evenodd. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.filter.note: grayscale(), sepia(), saturate(), hue-rotate(), brightness(), contrast(), invert() and opacity(), one after the other, on the colors of the element and of what it contains, the text of the terminal color taken as that of the color scheme and the terminal background kept; invert() alone swaps the foreground and background colors. drop-shadow() is the shadow of the box when box-shadow sets none, see box-shadow; blur() is accepted, a cell cannot be blurred; url() is not supported. On the shapes and groups of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them and their style attribute: these functions, blur() and drop-shadow() too, on their pixels, or url() of a <filter>, see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.flex.note: The grow and shrink factors, fractions too, and the basis.

css.properties.flex-basis.note: auto, content, lengths in columns and percentages of the row; a basis of 0 on an item that does not grow keeps its content width.

css.properties.flex-direction.note: The reverse directions lay the children out from the last; the focus order follows the document, like in CSS.

css.properties.flex-flow.note: The direction and the wrapping, see flex-direction and flex-wrap.

css.properties.flex-grow.note: Fractions too; factors summing to less than 1 share only that part of the free columns, like CSS; in a flex column of a set height, a least height, like min-height: 100vh, or stretched, the items that grow share its free rows, like a <main> of flex: 1 pushing a footer to the bottom.

css.properties.flex-shrink.note: Fractions too, weighing how much of the overflow each item takes with its width; 0 keeps the intrinsic width while others can give way.

css.properties.flex-wrap.note: In rows, wrap breaks the children that do not fit onto the next lines, measured by their content; wrap-reverse puts the lines from the bottom up; row-gap separates the lines.

css.properties.float.note: In a block container: the element at its left or right, at its width or its content's, the text of the blocks beside it flows around it, under it once it ends, aligned at its start, the paragraphs in blocks in them too (not those in flex rows, grids or scroll containers, laid out narrower beside it while they start beside it, like other boxes).

css.properties.flood-color.note: The color of an feFlood or an feDropShadow of a <filter>. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.flood-opacity.note: The opacity of an feFlood or an feDropShadow of a <filter>, a number or a percentage. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.font.note: The style, the weight, small-caps, the size, the line height after a slash and the families, see font-size and font-family; the longhands it does not set reset; the system fonts, like menu, set neither a size nor a family.

css.properties.font-family.note: The first FIGlet font of the list that is registered (big, small, slant, standard and mini are bundled), like font-family: slant, sans-serif; the others, like web fonts, are passed over, and generic families use the terminal font.

css.properties.font-feature-settings.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-language-override.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-optical-sizing.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-palette.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-size.note: Where the terminal draws text larger with the text sizing protocol of kitty (OSC 66), which the application tells with MediaContext::withTextSizing(): the text of a text block 2, 3 or 4 times as large, a size rounded to a whole number of times 16px (2em, 32px, xx-large, 200%), at most 4, each of its lines as many rows tall, the room of its line divided by it; the links of its text are followed by a click on the cells they take, and an element drawn over it hides it. Elsewhere, terminals have one font size.

css.properties.font-stretch.note: Terminals have one font: its width does not change.

css.properties.font-synthesis.note: The terminal draws bold and italic text with its own fonts; small capitals are Unicode characters, see font-variant-caps.

css.properties.font-synthesis-small-caps.note: The terminal draws bold and italic text with its own fonts; small capitals are Unicode characters, see font-variant-caps.

css.properties.font-synthesis-style.note: The terminal draws bold and italic text with its own fonts; small capitals are Unicode characters, see font-variant-caps.

css.properties.font-synthesis-weight.note: The terminal draws bold and italic text with its own fonts; small capitals are Unicode characters, see font-variant-caps.

css.properties.font-variant.note: small-caps draws lowercase letters as Unicode small capitals (ᴀʙᴄ), all-small-caps every letter; super and sub write the text with superscript or subscript characters, see font-variant-position; diagonal-fractions, ordinal and slashed-zero, see font-variant-numeric; the other values of the shorthand (ligatures, figures, alternates, east Asian forms, emoji) are accepted, the terminal choosing the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-variant-alternates.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-variant-east-asian.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-variant-emoji.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-variant-ligatures.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-variant-numeric.note: diagonal-fractions writes 1/2 as ½, and the other fractions with superscript and subscript digits (⁵⁄₁₆); ordinal writes the lowercase letters right after a number as superscript ones (1ˢᵗ, 2ⁿᵈ); slashed-zero draws 0 with a slash (0̸); the figure widths and styles (lining, oldstyle, proportional, tabular) and stacked fractions are left to the font of the terminal.

css.properties.font-variant-position.note: super and sub write the text with superscript or subscript characters when Unicode has all of them (digits, signs, most lowercase letters), like vertical-align on an inline element, which takes precedence; otherwise the text stays on the line.

css.properties.font-variation-settings.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.font-weight.note: 600 and above are bold, 300 and below dim (SGR 2); bolder and lighter are relative to the weight of the parent.

css.properties.font-width.note: Terminals have one font: its width does not change.

css.properties.forced-color-adjust.note: Forced colors draw no colors: none keeps the colors and gradients of the element, inherited by its descendants; preserve-parent-color is like auto.

css.properties.gap.note: One gap along the layout direction; grid-gap, its old name, too.

css.properties.grid.note: Like grid-template, or auto-flow [dense] [auto rows] / columns, or rows / auto-flow [dense] [auto columns], column after column.

css.properties.grid-area.note: An area name of grid-template-areas, or row-start / column-start / row-end / column-end lines.

css.properties.grid-auto-columns.note: The width of the columns past the explicit ones, its values taken in turn when it has several, like 10ch 20ch: lengths, percentages and minmax(); auto and fr are their content.

css.properties.grid-auto-flow.note: row places the items row after row, column column after column in the explicit rows (one without), adding columns; dense fills the free cells left before an item.

css.properties.grid-auto-rows.note: The least height of the rows past grid-template-rows, its values taken in turn when it has several, like 1fr 3ch: lengths, percentages and minmax(); auto and fr are their content.

css.properties.grid-column.note: Line numbers (negative ones count from the end), span N, auto and line names: name-start or name for a start, name-end or name for an end, the edges of a named area too; a name alone is both; name N (or N name) is the Nth line of the name, counted from the end when negative; span name (or span N name) reaches the Nth line of the name from the other line, auto without one.

css.properties.grid-column-end.note: Line numbers (negative ones count from the end), span N, auto and line names: name-start or name for a start, name-end or name for an end, the edges of a named area too; a name alone is both; name N (or N name) is the Nth line of the name, counted from the end when negative; span name (or span N name) reaches the Nth line of the name from the other line, auto without one.

css.properties.grid-column-start.note: Line numbers (negative ones count from the end), span N, auto and line names: name-start or name for a start, name-end or name for an end, the edges of a named area too; a name alone is both; name N (or N name) is the Nth line of the name, counted from the end when negative; span name (or span N name) reaches the Nth line of the name from the other line, auto without one.

css.properties.grid-row.note: Line numbers (negative ones count from the end), span N, auto and line names: name-start or name for a start, name-end or name for an end, the edges of a named area too; a name alone is both; name N (or N name) is the Nth line of the name, counted from the end when negative; span name (or span N name) reaches the Nth line of the name from the other line, auto without one.

css.properties.grid-row-end.note: Line numbers (negative ones count from the end), span N, auto and line names: name-start or name for a start, name-end or name for an end, the edges of a named area too; a name alone is both; name N (or N name) is the Nth line of the name, counted from the end when negative; span name (or span N name) reaches the Nth line of the name from the other line, auto without one.

css.properties.grid-row-start.note: Line numbers (negative ones count from the end), span N, auto and line names: name-start or name for a start, name-end or name for an end, the edges of a named area too; a name alone is both; name N (or N name) is the Nth line of the name, counted from the end when negative; span name (or span N name) reaches the Nth line of the name from the other line, auto without one.

css.properties.grid-template.note: none, rows / columns, and areas: each row a string of area names, its height after it, then / and the columns; line names are kept.

css.properties.grid-template-columns.note: Lengths, percentages of the width of the grid, also in calc(), min(), max() and clamp(), like minmax(min(20ch, 100%), 1fr), fr, auto, minmax() and repeat(), auto-fill and auto-fit, which drops the tracks no item is in, the others sharing their room; [line names] between the tracks, inside repeat() too, like repeat(auto-fill, [cell] 8ch), once per repetition; subgrid, the columns of the parent grid it spans, their widths and gap, which the content of its items, those of subgrids in it too, sizes, like rows of a table each a subgrid (not its line names, nor the margins, borders and padding of the subgrid at the edges of its tracks).

css.properties.grid-template-rows.note: Lengths and minmax() give the least height of a row, auto and fr its content; in a grid of a set height, the fr rows share its free rows as their fractions say; rows grow with their content, they are never cut; subgrid, the rows of the parent grid it spans and their gap, as tall as the content of its items and of the other items of those rows needs, like cards side by side whose titles, texts and links line up, its borders and padding above its first row and below its last (not its line names, nor its margins).

css.properties.hanging-punctuation.note: first: an opening bracket or quote starting a text block goes over its left padding; last: a closing one ending it over its right padding, the line before taking the last word when it then fits; as far as two columns of padding there are; aligned text is aligned with it; allow-end: a stop or a comma ending a line goes over the right padding when only it would not fit, the line keeping it; force-end is like allow-end.

css.properties.height.note: fit-content, max-content and min-content are the height of the content, like auto. In rows: the content is padded or clipped to it, a border-box height keeping a row for it when CSS leaves room for a line inside its border, like a field of 30px with a border of 1px; a percentage and a length, like calc(100% - 2rem), the length added to the share; a percentage of a parent of definite height (the root, or a fixed or percentage height) counts the border and padding, elsewhere it is ignored. On a <rect> of an <svg>, its height in user units, a unit or a percentage of the viewBox.

css.properties.hyphenate-character.note: auto, a hyphen, or a string, ending a line broken at a soft hyphen when it fits.

css.properties.hyphenate-limit-chars.note: With hyphens: auto, the fewest characters of a word broken at a soft hyphen, before the break and after it (the before one when missing); auto is no limit; inherited.

css.properties.hyphens.note: Soft hyphens (­) are where words break, showing the hyphenate-character there; none ignores them; auto also breaks the words without soft hyphens where the patterns of their language (lang) do: English, French, German and Spanish are bundled, other languages registered with HyphenatorRegistry::register(); a word split across inline elements is broken in each of them apart.

css.properties.image-orientation.note: from-image, the default, turns and flips a JPEG as the orientation of its EXIF data says, a photo taken sideways standing up; none draws it as stored; the deprecated angles and flip are taken as none.

css.properties.image-rendering.note: pixelated and crisp-edges scale images to their cells keeping the nearest pixel, like pixel art, sharp; auto and smooth average the pixels each half cell covers; in , background-image and list-style-image.

css.properties.initial-letter.note: On ::first-letter: a drop cap, the letter drawn in a bundled FIGlet font as many rows tall as its size (mini for 3, small for 4, standard for 5, big from 6, or the one its font-family names), the first lines of the text beside it; below 3 the letter alone, its lines kept; raise is like drop, nothing being drawn above the text.

css.properties.initial-letter-align.note: A drop cap is a FIGlet glyph whose top is that of the first line, see initial-letter.

css.properties.inline-size.note: Like width in a horizontal writing mode, like height in a vertical one.

css.properties.inset.note: One to four insets, like top, right, bottom and left, anchor() included.

css.properties.inset-block.note: The start and end insets, see inset-inline-start.

css.properties.inset-block-end.note: Like left, right, top and bottom; right to left, the inline start is the right.

css.properties.inset-block-start.note: Like left, right, top and bottom; right to left, the inline start is the right.

css.properties.inset-inline.note: The start and end insets, see inset-inline-start.

css.properties.inset-inline-end.note: Like left, right, top and bottom; right to left, the inline start is the right.

css.properties.inset-inline-start.note: Like left, right, top and bottom; right to left, the inline start is the right.

css.properties.interactivity.note: inert: like the inert attribute, the element and what it holds, which inherits it, take neither the focus nor the pointer, what is behind them taking the pointer; auto, the default, takes them back.

css.properties.interpolate-size.note: allow-keywords: a height transitions from or to auto, fit-content, min-content or max-content, through the height of the content in the last frame; not the widths.

css.properties.isolation.note: isolate makes the element a group of its own: the mix-blend-mode of what it contains blends with its background, or with nothing when it has none, not with what is behind it.

css.properties.justify-content.note: start, center and end, each line of a wrapping row in the room it leaves; space-between, space-around and space-evenly in rows, and in flex columns of a set height; stretch is like start, as in flexbox.

css.properties.justify-items.note: The justify-self of the items of a grid.

css.properties.justify-self.note: A grid item in its area along the row: start, center and end at its content width, stretch (the default) the whole area; ignored outside grids. anchor-center centers an element placed next to its anchor across it, like align-self down it.

css.properties.left.note: In cells or percents of the containing block of an absolute or fixed element (top: 100% puts it below), also in calc(), min(), max() and clamp(), like left: calc(50% - 10ch); top and bottom also place a sticky one.

css.properties.letter-spacing.note: Lengths rounded to columns, a column from three quarters of one, so that the .1em of a page is none, between the characters of a run; negative values are 0.

css.properties.lighting-color.note: The shapes of an <svg> are not drawn with it, from a style sheet or an attribute: see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.line-break.note: anywhere breaks lines between any two characters, like word-break: break-all; loose, normal and strict are like auto: lines break at spaces and soft hyphens, without the rules of the languages that differ.

css.properties.line-clamp.note: On text blocks: at most that many lines, the last one ending with an ellipsis.

css.properties.line-fit-edge.note: A line is a row of cells, its height that of the text.

css.properties.line-height.note: Numbers, lengths and percentages are rounded to rows: line-height: 2 puts a blank row between the lines of a text block; normal and below 2, like the 1.5 to 1.75 of the text of many pages, none.

css.properties.list-style.note: The type, the position and a url() image, see list-style-image.

css.properties.list-style-image.note: A url() image is the marker, a row tall and as wide as it says, from 1 to 4 columns, in half blocks, before a space; the list-style-type when it cannot be loaded, with forced colors, or a gradient.

css.properties.list-style-position.note: outside, the default: the marker before the first line of an item, its other lines aligned after it; inside: the marker is the start of the text, the lines wrapping under it.

css.properties.list-style-type.note: A counter style: disc, circle, square, disclosure-open, disclosure-closed, decimal, decimal-leading-zero, lower/upper-alpha, lower/upper-latin, lower/upper-roman, lower-greek, cjk-decimal, the other predefined styles of CSS Counter Styles (the digits of arabic-indic, persian, devanagari, bengali, thai and the other scripts, armenian, georgian, hebrew, hiragana, katakana and their iroha order, cjk-earthly-branch and cjk-heavenly-stem, ethiopic-numeric, the Japanese, Korean and Chinese long forms), or one of a @counter-style rule (an unknown one is decimal); none, or a string.

css.properties.margin.note: Around the border, painted like the parent; percentages are of the width of the containing block, for every side, like padding. A negative top or bottom margin pulls a block over what is before or after it in block and flex column layouts, its cells over theirs but for its spaces on no background or the one it inherits, like its margin, collapsing with the others like CSS; in a row, a negative left or right margin pulls an item over the one before it, never before the row, or the first child of an item with nothing on its left pulls the item, like a link of a pagination; a negative margin of less than a cell, like -1px, is a cell on a side with a border, which joins the border before it, ┐ and ┌ making ┬, like the buttons of a group; a negative bottom margin of the last children of a box with a bottom border and no bottom padding draws their last row over that border, a line hidden in the color of the background opening it, like the active tab of the tabs of Bootstrap; negative left and right margins are 0 elsewhere. With no border nor padding between them, the negative margin of a first or last block collapses into that of its parent, pulling the parent; inside a border or padding, it is 0. On inline elements, the left and right margins. Vertical margins collapse in block layout like CSS, between siblings and between a parent and its first or last child when no border or padding separates them; not in flex columns. Horizontal auto margins take the free columns of a row, or center a narrower block; vertical ones take the free rows of a flex column of a set height, like margin-top: auto pushing a button to the bottom of a card, nothing growing in it, and are 0 elsewhere.

css.properties.margin-block.note: Around the border, painted like the parent; percentages are of the width of the containing block, for every side, like padding. A negative top or bottom margin pulls a block over what is before or after it in block and flex column layouts, its cells over theirs but for its spaces on no background or the one it inherits, like its margin, collapsing with the others like CSS; in a row, a negative left or right margin pulls an item over the one before it, never before the row, or the first child of an item with nothing on its left pulls the item, like a link of a pagination; a negative margin of less than a cell, like -1px, is a cell on a side with a border, which joins the border before it, ┐ and ┌ making ┬, like the buttons of a group; a negative bottom margin of the last children of a box with a bottom border and no bottom padding draws their last row over that border, a line hidden in the color of the background opening it, like the active tab of the tabs of Bootstrap; negative left and right margins are 0 elsewhere. With no border nor padding between them, the negative margin of a first or last block collapses into that of its parent, pulling the parent; inside a border or padding, it is 0. On inline elements, the left and right margins. Vertical margins collapse in block layout like CSS, between siblings and between a parent and its first or last child when no border or padding separates them; not in flex columns. css.properties.margin-block-end.note: Around the border, painted like the parent; percentages are of the width of the containing block, for every side, like padding. css.properties.padding-top.note: Lengths, the top and bottom ones a row from three quarters of one, like padding: .5rem 1rem none above and below, and percentages of the width of the containing block for every side, like CSS (an item of a row takes them of the row), calc() mixing them and min(), max() and clamp() over them, like max(1ch, 5%); on inline elements, the left and right padding, in their colors, percentages being 0.

css.properties.page-break-after.note: column (and page, always, left, right) starts a column before or after the element in a multi-column container, within its column count; avoid keeps it in the column of its neighbour.

css.properties.page-break-before.note: column (and page, always, left, right) starts a column before or after the element in a multi-column container, within its column count; avoid keeps it in the column of its neighbour.

css.properties.paint-order.note: normal, or the order the fill, the stroke and the markers of a shape are drawn in, those left out after the others; text is drawn with its fill only. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.perspective.note: Cells cannot be rotated nor scaled: there is no 3D space; see translate.

css.properties.perspective-origin.note: Cells cannot be rotated nor scaled: there is no 3D space; see translate.

css.properties.place-content.note: Sets align-content from its first value and justify-content from its second one (or both from its only one): start, center, end, stretch and space-*.

css.properties.place-items.note: Sets align-items: start, center, end and stretch, and justify-items, its second value or its only one.

css.properties.place-self.note: align-self, then justify-self (or both from one value).

css.properties.pointer-events.note: none lets clicks and hover through to the element behind, see HtmlView::widgetAt(); the SVG values are auto.

css.properties.position.note: relative stays in the flow and contains the absolute elements inside it, its offsets moving it within its parent, its room kept empty (block elements, not inline ones); absolute and fixed leave the flow and are drawn over the rest at their insets from the closest positioned ancestor or the screen, or where they would be in the flow without insets, like a dropdown menu under its button, their blank cells without a background of their own showing what is under them, like a floating label over its field, an absolute ::before or ::after too (not the lists of controls, dialogs nor popovers, on the background of the page), sized by their content or both insets, inline elements too, like a badge in a paragraph, the text around them flowing on; sticky with top or bottom keeps the element in view in its scroll container, below its top or above its bottom, while its parent is, or its table for a cell, a row or a row group, like a header.

css.properties.position-anchor.note: The anchor-name an absolute or fixed element is placed next to, by position-area or anchor() in its insets.

css.properties.position-area.note: Next to the anchor: top, center or bottom, then left, center, right, span-left, span-right or span-all (one keyword is centered the other way), and the logical keywords (x-start, block-end, span-inline-start, start end, self-...), from the left and the top; the element is at its content width.

css.properties.position-try.note: An order, see position-try-order, then the fallbacks, see position-try-fallbacks.

css.properties.position-try-fallbacks.note: flip-block and flip-inline: the other side of the anchor when the element would leave the screen; then the @position-try rules named and the position-area values listed, in order, the first that fits on the screen, their insets or position-area replacing the insets of the element (their insets, position-area, position-anchor, width and height; not their margins).

css.properties.position-try-order.note: most-width and most-height, and their logical names most-inline-size and most-block-size: the position-try-fallbacks are tried by the room they leave next to the anchor, its width or its height, the most first, the element's own place still before them.

css.properties.position-visibility.note: always; anchors-visible, the initial value: an anchored element is not drawn while its anchor is not, like scrolled out of view or hidden; anchors-valid: nor when it has no anchor; no-overflow: nor when it does not fit on the screen, its fallbacks tried.

css.properties.quotes.note: auto, the marks of the language of the element (lang, inherited: « » in French, „ “ in German, 「 」 in Japanese...; English ones for the others), none, or pairs of strings by nesting level, for open-quote and close-quote.

css.properties.r.note: The radius of a <circle>. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.reading-flow.note: The order Tab and Shift+Tab follow through the children of the element, and what is inside them: flex-visual and grid-rows by rows of the last frame, then from the left, grid-columns by columns, flex-flow and grid-order by order then as written, source-order as written; positive tabindex values come first still.

css.properties.reading-order.note: In a reading-flow container, the children of a smaller one come first.

css.properties.resize.note: The size of a textarea follows its rows and its content.

css.properties.right.note: In cells or percents of the containing block of an absolute or fixed element (top: 100% puts it below), also in calc(), min(), max() and clamp(), like left: calc(50% - 10ch); top and bottom also place a sticky one.

css.properties.row-gap.note: Used when it matches the layout direction; grid-row-gap and grid-column-gap, their old names, too.

css.properties.ruby-align.note: Where an annotation narrower than its base is over it, and a base narrower than its annotation under it, the room shared on both sides: start at the start, the others centered, the spaces between the characters not stretched.

css.properties.ruby-position.note: over: the annotations of a ruby on a row above the line of their bases, under: on a row below it; alternate is like over, and inter-character too, an annotation not being drawn beside each character.

css.properties.rx.note: The radius of an <ellipse>, or of the corners of a <rect>. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.ry.note: The radius of an <ellipse>, or of the corners of a <rect>. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.scroll-behavior.note: smooth: the content of a scroll container glides to where it is scrolled, down or sideways, by the wheel, the keys, a target or the focus, in about 150 ms; at once with prefers-reduced-motion.

css.properties.scroll-initial-target.note: nearest: its scroll containers start scrolled to it, after the focus is first given, the first element of the document a rule or its style attribute sets it on, in any media or state; a later rule setting none back is not seen, and the page changing does not scroll again.

css.properties.scroll-margin.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-block.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-block-end.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-block-start.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-bottom.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-inline.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-inline-end.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-inline-star.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-left.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-right.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-margin-top.note: The rows and columns kept around an element when it is scrolled into view, as a target or as it takes the focus.

css.properties.scroll-marker-group.note: before or after: the ::scroll-marker of the children of a scroll container on a row inside it, before or after the content, styled by ::scroll-marker-group; a click on one scrolls to its child; they do not take the focus.

css.properties.scroll-padding.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-block.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-block-end.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-block-star.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-bottom.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-inline.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-inline-end.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-inline-sta.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-left.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-right.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-padding-top.note: The rows and columns of a scroll container kept clear at its sides when a target (:target) or the focus is scrolled into view, like under a sticky header.

css.properties.scroll-snap-align.note: The block value, then the inline one: start, center or end of the child at the same place of the scroll container, its scroll-padding and the scroll-margin of the child kept clear.

css.properties.scroll-snap-stop.note: always: a scroll stops at the child rather than going past it.

css.properties.scroll-snap-type.note: A scroll container snaps down (y, block), sideways (x, inline) or both ways to its children with a scroll-snap-align once scrolled, by the wheel, the keys or scrollTo(): mandatory always, to the snap position nearest the one asked in the way it went, proximity when one is within a third of its size.

css.properties.scroll-target-group.note: The links of a group are not scroll markers: see ::scroll-marker for the markers of a scroll container.

css.properties.scroll-timeline.note: A named timeline of the scroll container, or of the element in its scroll container, which animation-timeline names in the element and its descendants; block, inline, y or x.

css.properties.scroll-timeline-axis.note: A named timeline of the scroll container, or of the element in its scroll container, which animation-timeline names in the element and its descendants; block, inline, y or x.

css.properties.scroll-timeline-name.note: A named timeline of the scroll container, or of the element in its scroll container, which animation-timeline names in the element and its descendants; block, inline, y or x.

css.properties.scrollbar-color.note: The thumb and the track colors.

css.properties.scrollbar-gutter.note: stable keeps the column of the scrollbar of a scroll container even when its content fits, so that nothing moves when it overflows; both-edges keeps no column on the left.

css.properties.scrollbar-width.note: none hides the scrollbar, the content still scrolls; thin draws it with light lines.

css.properties.shape-image-threshold.note: The opacity, from 0 to 1 or a percentage, past which the pixels of a shape-outside image are part of the shape.

css.properties.shape-margin.note: The room kept around the shape of a float, a length like 1em, not a percentage; within its margin box, which the shape is clipped to.

css.properties.shape-outside.note: On a float, the text beside it wraps around its shape, row by row, the float itself drawn whole under the text that comes over it: circle(), ellipse(), inset() with round corners and polygon(), in the margin box or in the box named, like circle() border-box, the box alone too (its corners square); a url() image its pixels more opaque than shape-image-threshold, at its size from the top left of the box (one that cannot be read, or a gradient, gives the box); floats beside each other stay side by side by their boxes.

css.properties.shape-rendering.note: The shapes of an <svg> are not drawn with it, from a style sheet or an attribute: see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.speak.note: Nothing is spoken: screen readers read the terminal.

css.properties.stop-color.note: The color of a <stop> of a gradient. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stop-opacity.note: The opacity of a <stop> of a gradient, a number or a percentage. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stroke.note: A color, currentColor, none, or a pattern by url(), or a gradient drawn in its average color. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stroke-dasharray.note: none, or lengths in user units, px or percentages, the dashes and the gaps between them along the stroke, repeated; an odd list is taken twice. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stroke-dashoffset.note: Where the dashes start along the stroke, in user units, px or a percentage.
