On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stroke-linecap.note: butt, round or square: the ends of open lines and dashes. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stroke-linejoin.note: miter, round or bevel: the corners of a stroke at least two pixels wide; miter-clip and arcs are drawn like miter. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stroke-miterlimit.note: A number of 1 or more: a miter longer than that many widths of the stroke is bevelled. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stroke-opacity.note: A number or a percentage. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.stroke-width.note: In user units, px or a percentage. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.tab-size.note: In preserved whitespace, the columns between tab stops: a number of spaces, or a length rounded to columns.

css.properties.table-layout.note: fixed, on a table with a width (or a max-width, which width is here): the columns take the widths of the <col> elements, then of the cells of the first row, the others sharing what is left evenly; the rows after the first are not measured. Without a width, like auto.

css.properties.text-align.note: Each line of a text block is aligned, justify stretching the spaces of all but the last line of a paragraph; other widgets move their content as one block; match-parent takes the alignment of the parent, its start and end on the sides of its direction.

css.properties.text-align-last.note: The last line of each paragraph of a text block, and a paragraph of one line within the widest.

css.properties.text-anchor.note: start, middle or end: where the text of a <text> is at its x. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.text-autospace.note: A space between ideographs (Han, kana, bopomofo) and Latin, Greek or Cyrillic letters (ideograph-alpha) or digits (ideograph-numeric), across inline elements too: a whole column, where browsers add an eighth of an em, so the initial value is no-autospace and normal or auto turns it on; punctuation, insert and replace are accepted.

css.properties.text-box.note: A line of text is a row of cells: there is no space above or below its glyphs to trim.

css.properties.text-box-edge.note: A line of text is a row of cells: there is no space above or below its glyphs to trim.

css.properties.text-box-trim.note: A line of text is a row of cells: there is no space above or below its glyphs to trim.

css.properties.text-combine-upright.note: In a vertical writing mode, every character is upright, one a row: none is combined with others.

css.properties.text-decoration.note: underline, line-through, overline (SGR 53, drawn by kitty, WezTerm, VTE and others) and none, with the style and color of the underline; the thickness is accepted, the terminal drawing the line of its font.

css.properties.text-decoration-color.note: The color of the underline (SGR 58), in the terminals that draw it.

css.properties.text-decoration-inset.note: A line under or through text is as long as its cells: a fraction of one cannot be left out.

css.properties.text-decoration-skip.note: The terminal draws the underline of its font.

css.properties.text-decoration-skip-ink.note: The terminal draws the underline of its font.

css.properties.text-decoration-style.note: solid, double, wavy (curly), dotted and dashed underlines, in the terminals that draw them; the others draw a plain underline.

css.properties.text-decoration-thickness.note: The terminal draws the underline of its font.

css.properties.text-emphasis.note: The style and the color, see text-emphasis-style and text-emphasis-color.

css.properties.text-emphasis-color.note: The color of the marks, that of the text by default.

css.properties.text-emphasis-position.note: over or under the line; left and right, for vertical writing modes, are ignored.

css.properties.text-emphasis-style.note: none, filled or open dot (•◦), circle (●○, the default shape), double-circle (◉◎), triangle (▲△) and sesame (﹅﹆), or a string, its first character. The marks are on a row above the line (under: below it), over each character but the spaces and the punctuation, like a ruby annotation; a line that cannot have rows above it, like a button, has none.

css.properties.text-indent.note: Lengths and percentages of the width of the text block, hanging and each-line; a line pulled out by a negative length goes over the left padding, as far as there is; when a line is pulled out, the first line wraps as narrow as the others; one line pulled out further than the block is wide shows past the pull, like the text of a link replaced by a logo, which shows none; a first line pushed in as far as the block is wide holds its first word out of sight.

css.properties.text-justify.note: How text-align: justify fills the lines: inter-word stretches the spaces between words, inter-character (and distribute) the room between their characters too, none does not justify, auto like inter-word, and like inter-character for a line without spaces of wide (CJK) characters.

css.properties.text-orientation.note: Every character is upright in a vertical writing mode, one a row: a cell does not turn.

css.properties.text-overflow.note: clip, ellipsis (…) or a string, on lines that do not wrap.

css.properties.text-rendering.note: The terminal chooses the glyphs of its font.

css.properties.text-shadow.note: Up to 4 shadows, the first one over the others, each moved by whole cells (up to 2 each way), in its color or the text dimmed, under the text and showing only around it, not through the spaces between its words; the blur is ignored and a shadow under the text, without an offset, is not drawn.

css.properties.text-spacing-trim.note: A fullwidth punctuation mark takes two whole columns: half of it cannot be trimmed.

css.properties.text-transform.note: none, or a case (uppercase, lowercase, capitalize) with full-width (the ASCII characters as their full-width forms) and full-size-kana (small kana as their full-size forms), one after the other.

css.properties.text-underline-offset.note: The terminal draws the underline of its font.

css.properties.text-underline-position.note: The terminal draws the underline of its font.

css.properties.text-wrap.note: nowrap keeps a text block on one line; balance makes its lines as even as possible; pretty keeps the last line of a paragraph from holding a single word, when a narrower width does it without adding a line; stable is like wrap.

css.properties.timeline-scope.note: The names of timelines defined inside the element that its descendants see, like a progress bar beside the scroll container it follows.

css.properties.top.note: In cells or percents of the containing block of an absolute or fixed element (top: 100% puts it below), also in calc(), min(), max() and clamp(), like left: calc(50% - 10ch); top and bottom also place a sticky one.

css.properties.transform.note: translate(), translateX(), translateY() and the x and y of translate3d() move the element like relative offsets, its room kept: lengths, and percentages of the element itself, like translate(-50%, -50%) to center it, mixed with lengths in calc() too; scale(), rotate(), skew(), matrix() and perspective() are accepted and change nothing, cells being neither scaled nor turned, like the scale(1.05) of a card.

css.properties.transform-box.note: Cells cannot be rotated nor scaled: there is no 3D space; see translate.

css.properties.transform-origin.note: Cells cannot be rotated nor scaled: there is no 3D space; see translate.

css.properties.transform-style.note: Cells cannot be rotated nor scaled: there is no 3D space; see translate.

css.properties.transition.note: Each property with its duration, timing and delay, or all: colors and numbers go from the old value to the new one, also in lists and functions of the same shape (1ch 2ch, translate(), a shadow and its color, a gradient), lengths of different units through calc(); other values change at once, or halfway with allow-discrete, see transition-behavior.

css.properties.transition-behavior.note: allow-discrete: the values that cannot be interpolated change halfway, visibility staying visible while one end is; normal: they change at once.

css.properties.translate.note: Lengths and percentages of the element itself, like transform: translate().

css.properties.unicode-bidi.note: embed, isolate, bidi-override, isolate-override and plaintext set an inline element apart for the bidirectional algorithm, in its direction, like the controls of Unicode around it; plaintext on a text block takes its direction from its first strong character; with ext-intl or symfony/polyfill-intl-char.

css.properties.vector-effect.note: The shapes of an <svg> are not drawn with it, from a style sheet or an attribute: see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.vertical-align.note: On table cells, top, middle (the default of td and th, like HTML) and bottom place the content in the height of the row, or of the rows a cell spans; baseline is like top. On inline elements, super and sub write their text with superscript or subscript characters, when Unicode has all of them (digits, signs, some letters); the other values, lengths and percentages keep the text on the line.

css.properties.view-timeline.note: A named timeline of the scroll container, or of the element in its scroll container, which animation-timeline names in the element and its descendants; block, inline, y or x.

css.properties.view-timeline-axis.note: A named timeline of the scroll container, or of the element in its scroll container, which animation-timeline names in the element and its descendants; block, inline, y or x.

css.properties.view-timeline-inset.note: Lengths moving the edges of the scroll container in, for the view timeline; auto is 0.

css.properties.view-timeline-name.note: A named timeline of the scroll container, or of the element in its scroll container, which animation-timeline names in the element and its descendants; block, inline, y or x.

css.properties.view-transition-class.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.properties.view-transition-name.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.properties.visibility.note: hidden keeps the room and draws nothing, collapse frees it; a visible descendant of a hidden element stays hidden, and neither can take the focus.

css.properties.white-space.note: normal, nowrap (truncates), pre, pre-wrap, pre-line and break-spaces (like pre-wrap), and the pairs of white-space-collapse and text-wrap-mode, like preserve nowrap; nowrap on an inline element keeps its words on one line, unless longer than it; on a textarea, pre and nowrap keep each line on one row, scrolled sideways to the cursor.

css.properties.white-space-collapse.note: collapse, preserve and preserve-breaks, with text-wrap-mode, like the white-space values they make; break-spaces and preserve-spaces are like preserve.

css.properties.widows.note: The fewest lines of a text block at the top of the next column of a multi-column container when it is cut, 2 by default: otherwise lines go with them.

css.properties.width.note: A percentage takes that share of a row before flexible siblings, a growing item growing from it, its basis, like the width: 1% of the field of an input group of Bootstrap; inside a box sized by its content, a percentage is auto, like CSS; an absolute or fixed element takes it of its containing block; a flex item of a row that grows or has a basis takes the share of the row past its width, like the w-0 flex-1 of Tailwind; elsewhere width acts as max-width: widgets shrink to the room they get. fit-content and max-content make the box as wide as its content, fit-content(20ch) up to that length, min-content as narrow as it can be without overflowing, stretch (and -webkit-fill-available) take the room, like auto. On a <rect> of an <svg>, its width in user units, a unit or a percentage of the viewBox.

css.properties.will-change.note: A hint for browsers, without effect here.

css.properties.word-break.note: break-all breaks lines between any two characters; keep-all keeps the letters of Chinese, Japanese and Korean words together, lines breaking at spaces and punctuation, a word longer than the line still broken; auto-phrase is like normal.

css.properties.word-spacing.note: Lengths rounded to columns, a column from three quarters of one, added to each space between the words of a text block or of an inline element, the space before an element taking the spacing around it; negative values are 0.

css.properties.word-wrap.note: Words longer than the line are always broken, like anywhere and break-word: a terminal line cannot overflow.

css.properties.writing-mode.note: vertical-rl and vertical-lr turn the text of a text block: its lines are columns, from the right (or from the left), one character a row, as many rows as its height or the room; its logical sides and sizes are physical ones, the inline start at the top; sideways-rl and sideways-lr like vertical ones, the characters upright, cells not turning; the blocks of a block written vertically are its columns, from the right (or from the left), each as wide as its own, the block as wide as them unless its width is set; the row of a flex container runs down and its column from the right, like the axes of the text; the columns of a grid run down and its rows from the right (or from the left): grid-template-columns, grid-auto-columns, grid-column and column-gap are along the height, a length of a column in rows as many as its cells (8ch is 8 rows, 8 characters), and the rows, their areas, gaps, flow and alignments are turned likewise, the grid as wide as its rows unless its width is set; the text of an item in a column of a set length, or in an fr one of a grid of a set height, has lines as long as that column, in an auto one as long as the height of the grid or the screen; a percentage column is sized by its content, auto-fill and auto-fit columns repeat once (rows fill a set width, else repeat once), and direction: rtl does not turn the columns of a grid upward; its links are followed by a click where they are drawn, down their column.

css.properties.x.note: The corner of a <rect>, or where a <text> starts. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.y.note: The corner of a <rect>, or the baseline of a <text>. On the shapes of an <svg>, from its presentation attributes, the rules that match them, without states, in the media of the terminal, drawn again as it changes, and their style attribute, inherited, var() taking the custom properties of what holds them; see html.elements.svg.

css.properties.z-index.note: Orders the absolute and fixed elements drawn over the flow, a negative one drawn under the flow instead, the text of the page over its background, and not taking the pointer; the relative elements of a container moved by their offsets over each other, the higher one over the others, and those of a positive z-index drawn with the absolute and fixed ones, by z-index, their lines joined with those under them, like the active link of a pagination; the other elements in the flow are under the absolute and fixed ones of z-index 0 and more; a positioned element of a z-index other than auto is a stacking context, like one of opacity below 1, a filter, a blend mode, a transform or isolation: isolate: the positioned elements inside it are ordered among themselves and drawn with it, a negative one over its background and under its text, a z-index of 100 in one of 1 under a sibling of 2; a stacking context in the flow is drawn with the flow, whatever its z-index; the pointer follows the same order; the items of a grid that overlap are painted by it too, positioned or not.

css.selectors.active.note: The widget a pointer button is pressed on and its ancestors, from HtmlView::press() until HtmlView::release() or click(), or the "active" state the application sets; Enter or Space on the focused control makes it active for 0.15 s, terminals not reporting key releases.

css.selectors.active-view-transition.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.selectors.active-view-transition-typ.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.selectors.after.note: On text blocks, inline elements and blocks holding blocks (a line of its own), and as items of flex rows and grids, with content, in its colors and text attributes over those of its element, its horizontal padding in its background; absolute or fixed, of a block, drawn over the frame like an absolute element, the block its containing block when positioned, like a tooltip in .tip:hover::after, written :after too, like CSS 2.

css.selectors.autofill.note: Fields are never filled in by the terminal.

css.selectors.backdrop.note: Of a modal dialog: its background, translucent or not, is laid over what is under the dialog, the terminal background showing through but for an opaque one; opacity alone dims it; no other property.

css.selectors.before.note: On text blocks, inline elements and blocks holding blocks (a line of its own), and as items of flex rows and grids, with content, in its colors and text attributes over those of its element, its horizontal padding in its background; absolute or fixed, of a block, drawn over the frame like an absolute element, the block its containing block when positioned, like a tooltip in .tip:hover::after, written :before too, like CSS 2.

css.selectors.checked.note: Matches when the widget sets the "checked" state.

css.selectors.checkmark.note: The → of the selected option of a <select>, in a dropdown or a list: its colors and text attributes, and its content, none hiding it; not the boxes of a multiple one.

css.selectors.condensed.note: Tui extension: the effective density, from data-density or the media context.

css.selectors.cue.note: Videos and their captions are not played.

css.selectors.default.note: The first submit button of a form, and the checkboxes and radios with the checked attribute, checked or not since, and the options of a customizable <select> with the selected attribute; not the options of a plain <select>, which are not elements.

css.selectors.defined.note: Matches every element: there are no undefined custom elements.

css.selectors.details-content.note: The content of a <details>, styled like a box while it is open; the pseudo-classes after it apply to the content.

css.selectors.dir.note: The dir attribute of the element or of its closest ancestor setting ltr, rtl or auto (the direction of its first strong character).

css.selectors.file-selector-button.note: A file input is a path typed in, without a button.

css.selectors.first-letter.note: On text blocks: the first letter with the punctuation before it; colors and text attributes only; written :first-letter too, like CSS 2.

css.selectors.first-line.note: On text blocks: the first line as wrapped, under the styles of the inline elements on it; colors and text attributes only; written :first-line too, like CSS 2.

css.selectors.focus-visible.note: Same as :focus: focus always comes from the keyboard.

css.selectors.fullscreen.note: The view fills the terminal already.

css.selectors.future.note: Videos and their captions are not played.

css.selectors.grammar-error.note: Text is not checked for grammar.

css.selectors.heading.note: The h1 to h6 elements, or those of the levels listed, like :heading(2, 3).

css.selectors.highlight.note: The texts registered with HtmlView::highlight(name, texts), found in each text block across its inline elements: drawn in the colors and text attributes of the ::highlight(name) rules of the block over those of the text, a highlight registered later over the others; ranges are texts, scripts not running.

css.selectors.host.note: In the style sheets of a declarative shadow root: its host, the rules of the page winning over them whatever their specificity, but for important declarations, like the context of the cascade.

css.selectors.hostfunction.note: The host when it matches the selector; :host-context() when an ancestor does, not the host itself.

css.selectors.hover.note: The widget under the pointer and its ancestors, from HtmlView::hover() or the "hover" state, and the link of a text under it, like a:hover.

css.selectors.indeterminate.note: A <progress> without a value, and the radios of a group (a name in a form) of which none is checked; a checkbox when the application sets the "indeterminate" state, like the indeterminate IDL attribute.

css.selectors.lang.note: The lang attribute of the element or of its closest ancestor setting one, by language range, * matching any language; lang="" is no language.

css.selectors.marker.note: On <li>: its content, colors and text attributes, over those of the item; not its box.

css.selectors.namespace.note: *|type and *|* match like type and *; elements are in the HTML namespace and @namespace is ignored, so with any other prefix, or none (|type), a selector matches nothing.

css.selectors.nesting.note: Nested rules, the & selector and nested @media and @supports.

css.selectors.open.note: An expanded <details>, an open <dialog>, a <select> showing its list, or an <input list> showing its suggestions.

css.selectors.part.note: The elements of the shadow trees in what the selector before it matches with the parts named: the parts of a tree whose host is in the tree of the rule, and those their hosts export with exportparts.

css.selectors.past.note: Videos and their captions are not played.

css.selectors.paused.note: Every <video> and <audio>: they are not played, so always paused.

css.selectors.picker.note: ::picker(select): the list of a <select> drawn as a dropdown, styled like a box: border, padding, background, colors and the rest, as wide as its widest option with them; the pseudo-classes after it apply to the list.

css.selectors.picker-icon.note: The ▾ of a <select> drawn as a dropdown: its colors and text attributes, and its content, none hiding it.

css.selectors.placeholder.note: The hint of an empty <input> or <textarea>: its colors and text attributes, dimmed by the user agent stylesheet (opacity: 0.5), a transparent color hiding it, like the fields of the floating labels of Bootstrap; the pseudo-classes after it apply to the field.

css.selectors.playing.note: Never: audio and video are not played.

css.selectors.popover-open.note: A popover shown, by an invoker button or HtmlView::showPopover().

css.selectors.pseudo-element.note: Names a widget sub-element, like select::selected; the pseudo-classes after it apply to the widget.

css.selectors.read-only.note: Every element that is not :read-write, form controls and other elements alike.

css.selectors.read-write.note: Text inputs and textareas that are not readonly or disabled.

css.selectors.scope.note: Same as :root: style sheets are not scoped.

css.selectors.scroll-button.note: ::scroll-button(up), (down), (left), (right), their logical names and (*): the buttons of a scroll container with content, on a row inside it, the up one above the content, the others below, the left one at the start and the right one at the end; a click scrolls a page (85% of the viewport) that way, the button dim when it cannot; their colors and text attributes; they do not take the focus.

css.selectors.scroll-marker.note: On the children of a scroll container with scroll-marker-group: their marker in the group, its content, colors and text attributes; :target-current after it matches the one of the child scrolled to.

css.selectors.scroll-marker-group.note: The row of the markers: its colors and text attributes.

css.selectors.selection.note: The terminal selects text itself, in its own colors.

css.selectors.slotted.note: In the style sheets of a declarative shadow root: the elements of the page slotted in its slots, after a slot or not.

css.selectors.spelling-error.note: Text is not checked for spelling.

css.selectors.state.note: Tui extension: any other pseudo-class matches the widget state of that name, see AbstractWidget::setState().

css.selectors.target.note: The element a link to its fragment (<a href="#id">) was clicked to, or HtmlView::navigate() went to; it is scrolled into view, focused when it takes the focus.

css.selectors.target-current.note: The child of a scroll container whose ::scroll-marker is the current one, the last one that starts at where it is scrolled to or before (the last one shown at the end), like li::scroll-marker:target-current.

css.selectors.target-text.note: The text a text fragment goes to, like #:~:text=start,end or #id:~:text=prefix-,text,-suffix, from HtmlView::navigate() or a link: the first match of each text directive in a text block, whole words, the case not mattering, scrolled into view; in the colors and text attributes of its rules, those of a mark by default; not across text blocks.

css.selectors.valid.note: Constraint validation of <input>, <textarea> and checkboxes: required, minlength, maxlength, pattern (PCRE), and the email, url and number types; a <form> or a <fieldset> is invalid when a control inside is, like HTML.

css.selectors.view-transition.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.selectors.view-transition-group.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.selectors.view-transition-image-pair.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.selectors.view-transition-new.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.selectors.view-transition-old.note: Changes are drawn at once, without view transitions; see transition.

css.selectors.visited.note: A link followed, by its href, or one the application says it visited (HtmlView::setVisitedLinks()), styled in any property, a terminal having no history to keep from the page.

css.types.acos.note: An angle, like a hue in degrees; see calc().

css.types.anchor.note: The whole inset of an absolute or fixed element: a side of its anchor (top, right, bottom, left, center, start or end), the default one or the one named; no percentage side nor fallback, not in calc(); see position-anchor.

css.types.anchor-size.note: In width, height and their min- and max- of an absolute or fixed element: the width or height of its anchor (the default one or the one named), alone or in a math function linear in it, like calc(anchor-size(width) + 2ch), or the fallback without the anchor; one anchor-size() per value; not in margins nor insets.

css.types.angle.note: deg, grad, rad and turn: in gradients, hues, hue-rotate() and the trigonometric functions.

css.types.angle-percentage.note: Angles and percentages of a turn, in the stops of conic-gradient().

css.types.asin.note: An angle, like a hue in degrees; see calc().

css.types.atan.note: An angle, like a hue in degrees; see calc().

css.types.atan2.note: An angle, like a hue in degrees; see calc().

css.types.attr.note: In any property, of the element or the inline element: a string without a type (or raw-string), a value of the syntax of type(), a number, or a number with a unit; a fallback when the attribute is missing or not of the type, else the declaration is invalid at computed-value time. In content, a string.

css.types.basic-shape.note: circle(), ellipse(), inset() and polygon() in shape-outside; see clip-path.

css.types.blend-mode.note: normal, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, color-dodge, color-burn, hard-light, soft-light, difference, exclusion, hue, saturation, color and luminosity, with the formulas of the Compositing specification, on the colors of the cells; plus-lighter and plus-darker in mix-blend-mode.

css.types.calc.note: Over lengths, evaluated in cells after unit conversion; with width and max-width, percentages mix with lengths when the size stays a share plus columns, like calc(100% - 20ch) or calc((100% - 2ch) / 3).

css.types.calc-constant.note: e, pi, infinity, -infinity and NaN: NaN is 0, infinities are clamped to the largest size.

css.types.calc-keyword.note: e, pi, infinity, -infinity and NaN: NaN is 0, infinities are clamped to the largest size.

css.types.calc-size.note: In height, min-height and max-height: its basis, auto for a keyword, outside transitions; a transition to or from it computes it, size being the height of the content in the last frame, see interpolate-size.

css.types.color.note: Named colors, hexadecimal notations and the color functions; see css.types.color.*.

css.types.color.color.note: Out of the sRGB gamut, the chroma is lowered in OKLCH until clipping is not seen, like CSS gamut mapping; color() takes srgb, srgb-linear, display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, xyz, xyz-d50 and xyz-d65; translucent, blended like rgb().

css.types.color.color-mix.note: Two colors, in the space named (oklab by default) with the hue interpolation methods of the polar ones, premultiplied by their alpha; percentages summing to less than 100% make the mix translucent, blended like rgb().

css.types.color.color.relative_syntax.note: The channels of the origin color, in the space of the function, are keywords (r g b, h s l, l c h, x y z..., and alpha) usable in calc(), min(), max() and clamp().

css.types.color.contrast-color.note: White or black, whichever has the higher WCAG contrast ratio with the color.

css.types.color.currentcolor.note: The color of the element; ignored when no color is set.

css.types.color.hsl.note: A translucent color is blended over what is behind it: the closest background around the element (blended itself over the terminal background when translucent), its own background for its text, or the terminal background of the color scheme; transparent text takes the color behind it.

css.types.color.hsl.relative_syntax.note: The channels of the origin color, in the space of the function, are keywords (r g b, h s l, l c h, x y z..., and alpha) usable in calc(), min(), max() and clamp().

css.types.color.hwb.note: A translucent color is blended over what is behind it: the closest background around the element (blended itself over the terminal background when translucent), its own background for its text, or the terminal background of the color scheme; transparent text takes the color behind it.

css.types.color.hwb.relative_syntax.note: The channels of the origin color, in the space of the function, are keywords (r g b, h s l, l c h, x y z..., and alpha) usable in calc(), min(), max() and clamp().

css.types.color.lab.note: Out of the sRGB gamut, the chroma is lowered in OKLCH until clipping is not seen, like CSS gamut mapping; color() takes srgb, srgb-linear, display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, xyz, xyz-d50 and xyz-d65; translucent, blended like rgb().

css.types.color.lab.relative_syntax.note: The channels of the origin color, in the space of the function, are keywords (r g b, h s l, l c h, x y z..., and alpha) usable in calc(), min(), max() and clamp().

css.types.color.lch.note: Out of the sRGB gamut, the chroma is lowered in OKLCH until clipping is not seen, like CSS gamut mapping; color() takes srgb, srgb-linear, display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, xyz, xyz-d50 and xyz-d65; translucent, blended like rgb().

css.types.color.lch.relative_syntax.note: The channels of the origin color, in the space of the function, are keywords (r g b, h s l, l c h, x y z..., and alpha) usable in calc(), min(), max() and clamp().

css.types.color.named-color.note: All CSS named colors as true colors, except the 16 ANSI names (red, bright-red...) which keep the colors of the terminal theme; also Tailwind shades (emerald-500) and palette indexes (0-255).

css.types.color.oklab.note: Out of the sRGB gamut, the chroma is lowered in OKLCH until clipping is not seen, like CSS gamut mapping; color() takes srgb, srgb-linear, display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, xyz, xyz-d50 and xyz-d65; translucent, blended like rgb().

css.types.color.oklab.relative_syntax.note: The channels of the origin color, in the space of the function, are keywords (r g b, h s l, l c h, x y z..., and alpha) usable in calc(), min(), max() and clamp().

css.types.color.oklch.note: Out of the sRGB gamut, the chroma is lowered in OKLCH until clipping is not seen, like CSS gamut mapping; color() takes srgb, srgb-linear, display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, xyz, xyz-d50 and xyz-d65; translucent, blended like rgb().

css.types.color.oklch.relative_syntax.note: The channels of the origin color, in the space of the function, are keywords (r g b, h s l, l c h, x y z..., and alpha) usable in calc(), min(), max() and clamp().

css.types.color.rgb.note: A translucent color is blended over what is behind it: the closest background around the element (blended itself over the terminal background when translucent), its own background for its text, or the terminal background of the color scheme; transparent text takes the color behind it.

css.types.color.rgb.relative_syntax.note: The channels of the origin color, in the space of the function, are keywords (r g b, h s l, l c h, x y z..., and alpha) usable in calc(), min(), max() and clamp().

css.types.color.rgb_hexadecimal_notation.note: #rgb, #rrggbb, and #rgba and #rrggbbaa with an alpha channel, blended like rgb().

css.types.color.transparent.note: No color: what is behind shows; transparent text takes the color behind it.

css.types.cos.note: Of an angle (deg, grad, rad, turn) or a number of radians; see calc().

css.types.counter.note: counter(), in content, with a counter style.

css.types.counters.note: counters(), in content, with a separator and a counter style.

css.types.dimension.note: Lengths, angles, times and resolutions; see each of them.

css.types.easing-function.note: linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, cubic-bezier(), steps() and linear(); see css.types.easing-function.*.

css.types.easing-function.cubic-bezier.note: ease, ease-in, ease-out and ease-in-out too; outputs past 0 and 1 take numbers further, colors stay between.

css.types.easing-function.linear-functio.note: Stops with one or two input percentages, the missing ones spread evenly.

css.types.easing-function.steps.note: jump-start, jump-end, jump-none and jump-both, start, end, step-start and step-end.

css.types.env.note: The safe-area-inset, safe-area-max-inset and keyboard-inset variables are 0px: a terminal has no notch nor virtual keyboard; the others, like titlebar-area-x, take the fallback, without one the declaration is invalid at computed-value time; in every property and custom property.

css.types.flex.note: fr, in the tracks of a grid.

css.types.global_keywords.note: initial, inherit, unset, revert (to the user agent value) and revert-layer (like revert), in every property; see all.

css.types.gradient.note: linear-gradient(), radial-gradient(), conic-gradient() and their repeating forms, see background-image; the colors are interpolated in the space they name, like in oklch longer hue (sRGB by default), but for the colors of the terminal palette; translucent colors, transparent too, are interpolated premultiplied and blended over the background color of the box, else over what is behind it, which shows where the gradient is transparent.

css.types.gradient.conic-gradient.note: From an angle, around a position, like background-position, the center by default; stops with percentages or angles.

css.types.gradient.linear-gradient.note: An angle or to a side or corner, color stops with percentages or lengths; vertical distances count double, cells being twice as tall as wide.

css.types.gradient.radial-gradient.note: circle or ellipse, to the closest or farthest side or corner (farthest-corner by default) or of radii in lengths and percentages, at a position, like background-position; rows count double, cells being twice as tall as wide.

css.types.gradient.repeating-conic-gradi.note: The stops again and again past the last one; see conic-gradient().

css.types.gradient.repeating-linear-grad.note: The stops again and again past the last one; see linear-gradient().

css.types.gradient.repeating-radial-grad.note: The stops again and again past the last one; see radial-gradient().

css.types.if.note: The value of the first branch whose condition passes: else, or media(), supports() and style() tests (on the custom properties of the element) joined by not, and and or; without one passing, the declaration is invalid at computed-value time.

css.types.image.note: url() images, gradients and image-set(), in background-image, border-image-source, list-style-image, content and shape-outside; not cross-fade() nor element().

css.types.image.image-set.note: -webkit-image-set() too: the option of the lowest resolution not below the one of the screen (from the cell pixel size), else the highest, its size divided by it; options of a type() that cannot be decoded are left out; url(), a string or a gradient.

css.types.length.note: Unitless, ch and ex are columns, lh rows, and rch, rex and rlh alike; px are converted with the cell pixel size, the absolute units (pt, pc, in, cm, mm, Q) as their CSS pixels, 96 an inch; em and rem are 16px; vw, vh, vi, vb, vmin and vmax, and their small, large and dynamic forms (svh, dvh...), are shares of the screen, which does not change with toolbars; cqw, cqh, cqi, cqb, cqmin and cqmax are shares of the content box of the nearest container (inline-size or size for the width, size for the height), as laid out in the last frame, or of the screen without one; % for widths, heights, flex-basis, padding, margins and the insets of positioned elements.

css.types.percentage.note: Of the size of the containing block in widths, heights, paddings, margins and insets; of colors and of the stops of gradients. See css.types.length.

css.types.position.note: Keywords, lengths and percentages, one to four values with offsets from an edge, in background-position.

css.types.ratio.note: In aspect-ratio and in the aspect-ratio media feature, cells being twice as tall as wide.

css.types.ray.note: Boxes are not moved along paths; see offset-path.

css.types.resolution.note: dppx, x, dpi and dpcm, in the resolution media feature.

css.types.round.note: nearest, up, down and to-zero, to a multiple of a step, 1 (a cell) by default; see calc().

css.types.sibling-count.note: The number of elements of the parent of the element, itself included.

css.types.sibling-index.note: The position of the element among the elements of its parent, from 1, wherever a number is; inline elements count among the inline elements of their parent.

css.types.sin.note: Of an angle (deg, grad, rad, turn) or a number of radians; see calc().

css.types.string.note: In content, quotes and the other properties taking text.

css.types.system-color.note: Fixed colors of the light and dark color schemes, Canvas and CanvasText being the terminal background and text; AccentColor is the accent-color of the element when it sets one, AccentColorText the color that contrasts with it.

css.types.tan.note: Of an angle (deg, grad, rad, turn) or a number of radians; see calc().

css.types.text-edge.note: A line of text is a row of cells; see text-box-edge.

css.types.time.note: s and ms, in transitions and animations.

css.types.transform-function.note: translate(), translateX() and translateY(); see transform.

css.types.url.note: In @import, background-image, list-style-image, border-image-source, content and shape-outside, through the stylesheet loader, or data: URLs.

css.types.var.note: Custom properties in any property, with a fallback; see css.properties.custom-property.

html.elements.a.note: A terminal hyperlink (OSC 8) for http(s), mailto, file, ftp, sftp and ssh URLs, on each line it wraps over; a link to a fragment (#id) goes there when clicked, see :target. Text with links takes the focus (LinkedTextWidget, in the F6 cycle but never focused first): Tab and Shift+Tab, or Right and Left, move between its links, the current one reversed with the cursor on it, Enter follows it with a LinkEvent, which goes to a fragment and leaves the others to the application.

html.elements.area.note: The regions of the images whose usemap names its <map> are links: rect, circle, poly and default shapes, in CSS pixels of the image as drawn, the cells whose center is in them, the first area there winning; followed like the links of a text, to a fragment of the page or by the terminal; the image takes the focus (ImageMapWidget, in the F6 cycle but never focused first): Tab and Shift+Tab, or Right and Left, move between its areas, the current one reversed with the cursor on it, Enter follows it with a LinkEvent.

html.elements.audio.note: Not drawn: its fallback content is, like in browsers that cannot draw it, else the aria-label or the title in brackets, in the line of the text around it.

html.elements.b.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.base.note: href: the first absolute one is the URL the relative links (<a href>) are resolved against, for terminal hyperlinks and LinkEvent; links to a fragment stay in the page; not stylesheets, which the loader finds; target is ignored.

html.elements.bdi.note: Inline, isolated from the text around it (unicode-bidi: isolate), in the direction of its first strong character without dir; with ext-intl or symfony/polyfill-intl-char, otherwise drawn as stored.

html.elements.bdo.note: Inline, its characters in the order of its dir (unicode-bidi: isolate-override): dir="rtl" draws them right to left.

html.elements.big.note: Inline, bold: the font size cannot grow.

html.elements.button.note:
In the line of the text around it, like browsers, unless CSS displays it as a block; Enter or Space dispatches a PressEvent; the text content is the label, in brackets, unless CSS gives the button a border, which is then its look, or no border or a background, in rules of every state, like browsers, which then drop the native look; an icon in it is drawn in the line, a row tall, in the color of the button, its text alternative when it is too thin to show in so few cells; a submit button submits its form, see
.

html.elements.button.commandfor.note: With command: show-modal, close, request-close, show-popover, hide-popover and toggle-popover, each after a CommandEvent on the element, stopping it cancels the command; custom commands (--name) only dispatch the event.

html.elements.canvas.note: Not drawn: its fallback content is, like in browsers that cannot draw it, else the aria-label or the title in brackets, in the line of the text around it.

html.elements.center.note: A block whose text is centered.

html.elements.code.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.col.note: Not drawn: the width attribute (CSS pixels or a percentage) or the CSS width is the least width of each column it spans, span says how many; its background is under the cells of its columns without one; its other styles do not apply to them.

html.elements.colgroup.note: Not drawn: the width attribute (CSS pixels or a percentage) or the CSS width is the least width of each column it spans, span says how many; its background is under the cells of its columns without one; its other styles do not apply to them.

html.elements.data.note: Inline; its value attribute is kept for attribute selectors.

html.elements.datalist.note: For <input list>: the options containing what is typed are listed below the input while it has the focus (ComboboxWidget), Down (or Alt+Down) opens, all of them when none contains the value, Up and Down move, Enter takes, Escape hides them; the first one extending the value is shown after the cursor, Tab or Right takes it. A number field keeps stepping with Up and Down: Alt+Down opens its list.

html.elements.del.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.details.note: <summary>, open, and name for exclusive accordions; the content is the remaining children. The summary is matched like an element: its style, list-style: none, ::marker content and ::-webkit-details-marker { display: none } apply to its marker. Opening or closing it dispatches an ExpandEvent or a CollapseEvent, then a ToggleEvent.

html.elements.dfn.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.dialog.note: Shown when open, as a box in the flow: the "open" state (:open) is the attribute; HtmlView::show() opens it there and showModal() over the page, under its ::backdrop, both focusing its first control; close() closes it, with a return value (getReturnValue(), the value of the button that submits a form of method dialog in it), and dispatches a CloseEvent; Escape, a click outside one of closedby="any", request-close and requestClose() dispatch a CancelEvent first, which stopping keeps it open; a BeforeToggleEvent before it opens or closes, stopping it keeps it closed, and a ToggleEvent once it has.

html.elements.dialog.closedby.note: any: Escape or a click outside closes the dialog; closerequest: Escape does, the default of a modal one; none: neither, the default of the others.

html.elements.em.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.embed.note: An image (src, of no type or an image/ one) is drawn like an , width and height too; anything else is not: the aria-label or the title is shown in brackets in the line of the text around it, like an that cannot be drawn.

html.elements.fieldset.note: disabled disables the form controls inside, except those of its first <legend>.

html.elements.font.note: Inline; its color, size (1 to 7, or relative to 3 like +2, see font-size) and face (see font-family) attributes are presentational hints.

html.elements.form.note: A submit button or Enter in a single-line field submits it, after constraint validation (novalidate, formnovalidate): the FormWidget dispatches a FormSubmitEvent with the values of its named, enabled controls, a name ending with [] collecting a list, and its action and method (formaction and formmethod of the button first), the application sending them; method="dialog" closes the dialog the form is in; its controls are those it holds and those whose form attribute names it, before or after it; reset buttons restore the initial values.

html.elements.head.note: Not drawn: its <title>, <style> and <link> elements are read.

html.elements.html.note: The root: :root, its rules and its attributes, like lang and dir, apply; as tall as its content, its percentage heights and those of <body> are of the screen. HtmlView::getRoot() returns it, getBody() the <body>.

html.elements.i.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.iframe.note: srcdoc: a nested document in a box of its width and height (300 by 150 CSS pixels by default) with a border, scrolled when taller, styled by its own stylesheets only, which do not reach the page around it, its media queries and viewport units of that box inside its border (of its attributes, not of a CSS size); its fields join the focus order of the page; nested three deep at most. Without srcdoc, the document of its src, read like the src of an (a data: URL, or the loader given to ImageElement for iframe), as UTF-8; one that cannot be read: the aria-label, the title or the child is shown in brackets in the line of the text around it, like an <img> that cannot be drawn.

html.elements.img.note: Raster images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP... with the GD extension), and SVG ones drawn at their size, are drawn with half blocks in true colors, from a data: URL or through the loader given to ImageElement; width and height are CSS pixels (8 per column, 16 per row), CSS sizes bound them, a height alone narrowing it by its proportions; without a width its box is as wide as it is drawn, like the inline images of browsers. Inside an inline element, like a link, it is drawn in the line of the text, a row tall and as wide as its proportions say (up to 16 columns), wrapped like a word. Otherwise the alt text is shown in brackets in the line of the text around it, like browsers; an empty alt or aria-hidden shows nothing; srcset picks the candidate for the density of the terminal, like a <picture>, chosen again as it changes.

html.elements.input.note: Text-like types (text, search, email, url, tel, number with arrows stepping it, password masked), date, time, datetime-local, month and week as text validated against their format, range as a slider, checkbox and radio, submit, button and reset; value, placeholder, readonly, maxlength (typing and pasting stop at it), checked and name (radio groups). color as #rrggbb with a swatch of it (ColorInputWidget), file as a path to type in, completed like in a shell with Tab (the entries of its directory, the files of the types accept names, by extension or MIME type); hidden is not drawn, its value submitted; image is a submit button drawing its image a row tall, like the icon of a button (its alt its name, shown when the image cannot be drawn), sending name.x and name.y.

html.elements.input.size.note: A presentational hint: the width of a text field, in characters, the cursor's column added; without it, a field its content sizes, like in a flex row, is 20 characters wide, like browsers, not the room it has.

html.elements.input.type_checkbox.note: Space toggles it; the "checked" state follows the value; only the box is drawn, like in a browser.

html.elements.input.type_radio.note: Space checks it and unchecks the radios of the same name in the document.

html.elements.ins.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.kbd.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.label.note: Names its control, by for or by wrapping it; a click on the label goes to the control.

html.elements.legend.note: The first one of a <fieldset> is drawn in its top border, after its left corner, like browsers; without a top border, on a line of its own.

html.elements.li.note: The marker follows list-style-type, list-style-position and li::marker, while it is displayed as a list item: displayed otherwise, like a block or a flex row, it has none; an item with nested blocks is a container, its first block carrying the marker; displayed as a flex or grid container, its text and its elements are items.

html.elements.link.note: rel="stylesheet" only, loaded with the stylesheet loader; the media attribute is honored.

html.elements.map.note: Its content is drawn, like in a browser; its <area> elements make regions of the images that use it (usemap) links, see <area>.

html.elements.mark.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.marquee.note: Its text moves sideways on one line (MarqueeWidget): direction (left or right, up and down like them), behavior (scroll, slide, alternate), scrollamount (8 CSS pixels a column, a column at least), scrolldelay (60ms at least unless truespeed) and loop; still at its start with prefers-reduced-motion; a marquee holding blocks is a block, its text not moving.

html.elements.meta.note: name="color-scheme": the color-scheme of <html> under any CSS rule, from the first valid one; the other names and charset are ignored.

html.elements.meter.note: value, min and max, drawn as a bar and its percentage, which says it without colors, like <progress>; low, high and optimum set :optimum, :suboptimum or :even-less-good, green, yellow and red by default.

html.elements.noscript.note: Drawn, its style sheets applying, like in a browser without scripts: scripts do not run; left out, its style sheets too, once they do, see HtmlBuilder::setScripting().

html.elements.object.note: An image (data, of no type or an image/ one) is drawn like an , width and height too; anything else is not: its fallback content is, like in browsers that cannot draw it, else the aria-label or the title in brackets, in the line of the text around it.

html.elements.optgroup.note: Inside <select>: a heading over its options; disabled hides them.

html.elements.option.note: Inside <select>: see select. In a dropdown, an option holding elements and its elements are styled by CSS, like option:default or option .flag: their colors and text attributes, in the list and in the field.

html.elements.p.align.note: A presentational hint: text-align, on cells, rows, captions, paragraphs, divisions and headings.

html.elements.param.note: The parameters of an <object>: an image is drawn without them, anything else is not drawn.

html.elements.picture.note: The image of the first whose media query matches, else its , chosen again as the media change (the color scheme, the width...); each source is read like an with the candidate of its srcset for the density of the terminal (the smallest density at least its resolution, the densest past them; width descriptors over the px length of sizes or the width attribute, else the first candidate), through the factory and its loader.

html.elements.progress.note: value and max: the bar and its percentage, which says it without colors; without a value, indeterminate, the bar moving, still with prefers-reduced-motion; no step count, like a browser.

html.elements.rp.note: Hidden, like in browsers that draw ruby.

html.elements.rt.note: Over its base, see <ruby>; displayed inline, it is drawn after it, like in browsers.

html.elements.ruby.note: Its annotations (<rt>) on a row above the line of their bases, or below it with ruby-position: under, each base as wide as its annotation, kept on one line; bases (<rb>, or the text before the annotations) and annotations pair one to one, the annotations left over going with the last base; <rtc> is an annotation of its own; on a line that cannot have rows above it, like a button, the annotation follows its base in parentheses.

html.elements.s.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.samp.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.select.note: Without size or multiple, a dropdown (DropdownWidget): the choice on one line, Enter or Space opens the list over what follows, Enter takes an item, Escape or leaving it closes it as it was; with them, a list. <option> value, label, title (description), selected. <optgroup label> is a heading over its options, styled by select::group; a disabled one hides them.

html.elements.selectedcontent.note: Inside the <button> of a customizable <select>: the field shows the content of the selected option, its elements styled like in the list, the ▾ after it.

html.elements.slot.note: In a declarative shadow root, see <template>: the children of the host whose slot attribute names it (or without one, for the slot without a name), else its own content; display: contents, by the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.source.note: In a <picture>: media, srcset (the candidate for the density of the terminal, see <picture>), sizes as a px length, width and height; a source whose first candidate cannot be read or decoded is skipped; its other candidates are read when they are first drawn, their alt text shown when they cannot be, like browsers.

html.elements.strong.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.sub.note: Subscript characters (H₂O) when Unicode has all of them, see vertical-align; otherwise on the line.

html.elements.summary.note: In a <details>: its text, styled like an element (summary { ... }); its marker follows list-style: none, ::marker content and ::-webkit-details-marker; ::before and ::after content around its text, the latter at the end of the line in a flex row spread by justify-content, like the + of a FAQ.

html.elements.sup.note: Superscript characters (x²) when Unicode has all of them, see vertical-align; otherwise on the line.

html.elements.svg.note: With the GD extension, its shapes are drawn with half blocks in true colors, like an : rect (with rx and ry), circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon and path (every command, curves and arcs too), in groups, nested

html.elements.table.note: Columns are sized across the rows by their widest cell, shrunk down to their longest words when the table is too wide, and evenly past them, stretched by a percentage width; colspan spans columns; rowspan draws the cell across the rows it spans, the last of them taller when it needs more (in its first row when border-spacing sets rows apart).

html.elements.table.bgcolor.note: A presentational hint: the background color, of tables, rows and cells.

html.elements.table.border.note: A presentational hint: a border around the table, none for 0.

html.elements.table.width.note: A presentational hint: CSS pixels or a percentage, under any CSS rule.

html.elements.tbody.note: Columns are sized across the rows by their widest cell, shrunk down to their longest words when the table is too wide, and evenly past them, stretched by a percentage width; colspan spans columns; rowspan draws the cell across the rows it spans, the last of them taller when it needs more (in its first row when border-spacing sets rows apart).

html.elements.td.note: Columns are sized across the rows by their widest cell, shrunk down to their longest words when the table is too wide, and evenly past them, stretched by a percentage width; colspan spans columns; rowspan draws the cell across the rows it spans, the last of them taller when it needs more (in its first row when border-spacing sets rows apart).

html.elements.td.align.note: A presentational hint: text-align, on cells, rows, captions, paragraphs, divisions and headings.

html.elements.td.bgcolor.note: A presentational hint: the background color, of tables, rows and cells.

html.elements.td.width.note: A presentational hint: CSS pixels or a percentage, under any CSS rule.

html.elements.template.note: Not drawn, but with shadowrootmode (open or closed), as the first of its kind in an element: a declarative shadow root, its content drawn in place of the children of that element, which go in its <slot> elements; its <style> and <link> elements style it alone, and those of the page do not reach in but by inheritance, ::part() and the host; the child and sibling combinators of the page see a slotted element in its slot, not in its host. Scripts not running, nothing else uses templates.

html.elements.textarea.note: Content, rows (that many lines, scrolling past them, unless field-sizing: content; without it, it grows), placeholder, readonly and maxlength, and cols as a width in columns; wrap="off" keeps each line on one row, scrolled sideways to the cursor (like white-space: pre).

html.elements.textarea.cols.note: A presentational hint: width in columns, under any CSS rule.

html.elements.tfoot.note: Columns are sized across the rows by their widest cell, shrunk down to their longest words when the table is too wide, and evenly past them, stretched by a percentage width; colspan spans columns; rowspan draws the cell across the rows it spans, the last of them taller when it needs more (in its first row when border-spacing sets rows apart).

html.elements.th.note: Columns are sized across the rows by their widest cell, shrunk down to their longest words when the table is too wide, and evenly past them, stretched by a percentage width; colspan spans columns; rowspan draws the cell across the rows it spans, the last of them taller when it needs more (in its first row when border-spacing sets rows apart).

html.elements.thead.note: Columns are sized across the rows by their widest cell, shrunk down to their longest words when the table is too wide, and evenly past them, stretched by a percentage width; colspan spans columns; rowspan draws the cell across the rows it spans, the last of them taller when it needs more (in its first row when border-spacing sets rows apart).

html.elements.title.note: The title of the terminal window or tab, set when the view is mounted at the root of the Tui (HtmlView::getDocumentTitle() returns it); the terminal keeps it after the program stops.

html.elements.tr.note: Columns are sized across the rows by their widest cell, shrunk down to their longest words when the table is too wide, and evenly past them, stretched by a percentage width; colspan spans columns; rowspan draws the cell across the rows it spans, the last of them taller when it needs more (in its first row when border-spacing sets rows apart).

html.elements.track.note: Videos and their captions are not played.

html.elements.tui-columns.note: Tui extension: children laid out in columns, see .columns.

html.elements.tui-loader.note: Tui extension: a LoaderWidget; the text content is the message.

html.elements.tui-markdown.note: Tui extension: a MarkdownWidget rendering its text content.

html.elements.tui-tabs.note: Tui extension: a TabsWidget; each child is a tab labeled by its title.

html.elements.tui-text.note: Tui extension: a TextWidget; truncate="" truncates instead of wrapping.

html.elements.u.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.var.note: Inline: styled by CSS, see the user agent stylesheet.

html.elements.video.note: Not played: its poster is drawn like an , width and height too, else its fallback content is, like in browsers that cannot play it, else the aria-label or the title in brackets, in the line of the text around it.

html.elements.wbr.note: A line break opportunity: a long word can wrap there.

html.global_attributes.accesskey.note: Alt + the key focuses the element.

html.global_attributes.aria-describedby.note: Used as the description of <select> options and <details>.

html.global_attributes.autocapitalize.note: Text is typed as it is: there is no virtual keyboard.

html.global_attributes.autocorrect.note: Text is typed as it is: there is no virtual keyboard.

html.global_attributes.contenteditable.note: Elements cannot be edited in place: see <textarea> and <input>.

html.global_attributes.dir.note: Sets direction, see the CSS property, and isolates the element (unicode-bidi: isolate): rtl mirrors rows and logical sides, starts text on the right and draws it right to left; auto takes the direction of the first strong character.

html.global_attributes.enterkeyhint.note: Text is typed as it is: there is no virtual keyboard.

html.global_attributes.exportparts.note: On the host of a shadow tree in another: the parts of its tree the outer tree sees, like "icon, label: title", under their name or another, on out through the hosts that export them again.

html.global_attributes.inert.note: The subtree takes neither the focus nor the pointer.

html.global_attributes.inputmode.note: Text is typed as it is: there is no virtual keyboard.

html.global_attributes.interestfor.note: Pointing at the element or focusing it shows the popover it names, anchored to it (position-area places it), and leaving it hides it, unless the popover is pointed at; no delays.

html.global_attributes.is.note: There are no custom elements: the element is drawn like its tag.

html.global_attributes.lang.note: Kept for attribute selectors and :lang(), and the quotation marks of quotes: auto; the words that hyphens: auto breaks, see the CSS property; text is not otherwise localized.

html.global_attributes.nonce.note: Scripts do not run, and style sheets are not filtered by a content security policy.

html.global_attributes.part.note: The names of an element of a shadow tree that ::part() matches from outside it; kept for attribute selectors.

html.global_attributes.popover.note: auto, manual or hint: hidden until shown (:popover-open), then over the page, centered by the user agent stylesheet; an auto one closes on Escape, a click outside it and another auto one opening. Its invoker is its implicit anchor, which position-area and anchor() use. A hint one closes the other hints, not the auto ones, which close it. A BeforeToggleEvent is dispatched on it before it is shown or hidden, stopping it keeps it hidden, and a ToggleEvent once it is.

html.global_attributes.role.note: Kept for attribute selectors; status and alert are live regions.

html.global_attributes.slot.note: The <slot> of the shadow tree of its parent it is drawn in, by name; without it, the slot without a name.

html.global_attributes.spellcheck.note: Text is not checked for spelling.

html.global_attributes.style.note: Declarations take part in the cascade, var() included.

html.global_attributes.tabindex.note: Orders the F6 focus cycle; a negative value leaves the cycle.

html.global_attributes.title.note: Labels the widget, after aria-label and <label>; HtmlView::titleAt() returns it for tooltips.

html.global_attributes.writingsuggestion.note: Text is typed as it is: there are no suggestions.

mathml.elements.math.note: Drawn as linear text in the line of the text around it, display="block" on a line of its own, centered: x^2 for <msup>, x_i for <msub>, a/b for <mfrac>, √(x) for <msqrt>, the groups of several parts in parentheses; <annotation> is not drawn.
